== National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems ==
The mission which has a five-year budget of ₹3,660 crore, was authorized by the Union Cabinet in December 2018 under the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]]. A technological vertical in AI and ML, [[IoT]], [[data bank]] and [[DaaS]], [[data analysis]], autonomous systems and robotics, [[cyber security]], and [[quantum engineering]] has been assigned to each of the 25 technological innovation hubs that have been formed.<ref>{{Cite web |title=National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS) |url=https://nmicps.in/home/bannerimages/Quarterly_Bulletin_Oct_2023.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240901204014/http://nmicps.in/home/bannerimages/Quarterly_Bulletin_Oct_2023.pdf | publisher=Department of Science and Technology Ministry of Science and Technology | date=October 2023 |archive-date=2024-09-01 |access-date=2025-02-01 |website=nmicps.in}}</ref>

To translate academic research on AI at the proof-of-concept stage into commercially viable goods and services, IIT Kharagpur established the AI4ICPS Innovation Hub Foundation in 2020. Under the National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS), the Department of Science and Technology awarded it a grant of ₹170 crore.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Das |first=Sejuti |date=2020-11-25 |title=IIT Kharagpur Sets Up AI & ML Innovation Hub To Transform The Industrial Sector With Scalable Application |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/iit-kharagpur-sets-up-ai-ml-hub-to-transform-industrial-sector-with-scalable-application/ |access-date=2025-01-31 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=25 November 2020 |title=IIT Kharagpur Innovation Hub On AI, ML To Translate Research To Industrially Scalable Products |url=https://www.ndtv.com/education/iit-kharagpur-innovation-hub-on-ai-ml-translate-research-industrially-scalable-products-2330044 |access-date=2025-01-31 |website=ndtv.com |language=en}}</ref>

With a [[seed money]] of ₹230 [[crore]] from the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]] and the [[Government of Karnataka]], an Artificial Intelligence and Robotics Technology Park was established at the [[Indian Institute of Science]] as not-for-profit foundation in November 2020 for mission-mode research and development projects in cyber-security, healthcare, education, mobility, infrastructure, agriculture, and retail.<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 November 2020 |title=ARTPARK to usher in a new model of industry, academia and government collaboration in AI & Robotics for societal impact |url=https://pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1677000 |access-date=18 February 2025 |website=Press Information Bureau |agency=Ministry of Science & Technology, Government of India}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-14 |title=Artificial Intelligence and Robotics Technology Park launched in IISc Bengaluru |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/bangalore/artificial-intelligence-robotics-technology-park-launched-iisc-bengaluru-7819484/ |access-date=2025-02-18 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref> 

TiHAN at [[IIT Hyderabad]] hosted India's first Autonomous Navigations Testbed Facility (Aerial & Terrestrial) in 2022, which was opened by [[Jitendra Singh Rana]] from [[Ministry of Science and Technology (India)|Ministry of Science and Technology]] to develop next-generation autonomous navigation technology.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Luthra |first=Swati |date=2022-07-04 |title=India's first autonomous navigation facility, TiHAN, launched at IIT Hyderabad |url=https://www.livemint.com/news/india/indias-first-autonomous-navigation-facility-tihan-launched-at-iit-hyderabad-11656943204369.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240521041052/https://www.livemint.com/news/india/indias-first-autonomous-navigation-facility-tihan-launched-at-iit-hyderabad-11656943204369.html |archive-date=2024-05-21 |access-date=2025-02-07 |work=mint |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=5 July 2022 |title=TiHAN: India's first technology innovation hub on autonomous navigation facility launched at IIT Hyderabad - ET Auto |url=https://auto.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/auto-technology/tihan-indias-first-technology-innovation-hub-on-autonomous-navigation-facility-launched-at-iit-hyderabad/92681196 |access-date=2025-02-07 |website=ETAuto.com |language=en}}</ref>

To develop spectral and energy-efficient wireless communications technology for [[5G]] and [[5G-Advanced]], Kiran Kumar Kuchi of IIT Hyderabad and IIITB Comet Foundation in 2024 developed an O-RAN base station solution that triples capacity and improves cell coverage when compared to [[4G]] networks.<ref>{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2024-02-09 |title=IIITB COMET Foundation devises solution for better connectivity of advanced radio networks |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/karnataka/iiitb-comet-foundation-devises-solution-for-better-connectivity-of-advanced-radio-networks/article67828907.ece |access-date=2025-02-07 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

== Legislation ==

India currently does not have specific laws regulating artificial intelligence (AI). However, the Indian government has introduced several initiatives and guidelines aimed at the responsible development and deployment of AI technologies.<ref name="morganlewis">{{cite web |url=https://www.morganlewis.com/blogs/sourcingatmorganlewis/2024/01/ai-regulation-in-india-current-state-and-future-perspectives |title=AI Regulation in India: Current State and Future Perspectives |publisher=Morgan Lewis |access-date=2024-07-20}}</ref><ref name="indiabriefing">{{cite web |url=https://www.india-briefing.com/news/india-regulation-of-ai-and-large-language-models-31680.html/ |title=Regulation of AI and Large Language Models in India |date=27 March 2024 |publisher=India Briefing |access-date=2024-07-20}}</ref> The Indian government has tasked [[NITI Aayog]], its apex public policy think tank, with establishing guidelines and policies for AI. In 2018, NITI Aayog released the '''National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence''', also known as '''#AIForAll''', which focuses on healthcare, agriculture, education, [[smart cities]], and [[smart mobility]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 2018 |title=National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence |url=https://www.niti.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-03/National-Strategy-for-Artificial-Intelligence.pdf |access-date=23 January 2025 |website=NITI Aayog}}</ref>

In 2021, NITI Aayog published the "Principles for Responsible AI," addressing ethical considerations for AI deployment in India.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-14 |title=AI Job Crisis: AI की वजह से भारत में सबसे पहले कौन-कौन सी नौकरियां खत्म हो सकती हैं? |url=https://timelybharat.com/ai-job-crisis-india/ |access-date=2026-05-14 |language=en-US}}</ref> These principles cover system considerations, such as decision-making and accountability, and societal considerations, such as the impact of automation on employment. The second part of this document, "Operationalizing Principles for Responsible AI," released in August 2021, focuses on implementing these ethical principles through regulatory and policy interventions, capacity building, and incentivizing ethical practices.<ref name="morganlewis" /><ref name="indiabriefing" />

In 2023, the Indian government enacted the [[Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023|Digital Personal Data Protection Act]], which addresses some privacy concerns related to AI platforms. [[Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology|The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)]] has also issued advisories requiring platforms to obtain explicit permission before deploying unreliable AI models and to label AI-generated content to prevent misuse.<ref name="morganlewis" /><ref name="indiabriefing" /> India is a member of the [[Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence|Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence (GPAI)]], which promotes the responsible use of AI through international collaboration. In 2023, the GPAI Summit was held in New Delhi, where experts discussed responsible AI, data governance, and the future of work.<ref name="morganlewis" />

Other Indian agencies, such as the [[Bureau of Indian Standards|Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS)]], are also working on AI policies. BIS has established a committee to propose draft standards for AI, focusing on safety, reliability, and ethical considerations.<ref name="dataguidance">{{cite web |url=https://www.dataguidance.com/opinion/india-ai-regulation-current-state-and-future |title=India: AI regulation - current state and future perspectives |publisher=Data Guidance |access-date=2024-07-20}}</ref> India has not yet enacted specific AI regulations. However, the government has introduced measures to promote innovation and address ethical concerns and risks associated with AI. These efforts aim to support the growth of India's AI ecosystem and ensure responsible AI deployment.<ref name="indianexpress">{{cite web |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/business/india-will-regulate-ai-but-not-at-the-cost-of-innovation-govt-official-9335211/ |title=India will regulate AI, but not at the cost of innovation: Govt official |date=17 May 2024 |publisher=Indian Express |access-date=2024-07-20}}</ref>

== Bharat GPT initiative ==
The Bharat GPT is a non-profit initiative, started in February 2023.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Jindal |first=Siddharth |date=2024-03-18 |title=Everything You Need to Know About BharatGPT |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-features/everything-you-need-to-know-about-bharatgpt/ |access-date=2025-02-28 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref> The goal is to develop India focused [[Multilingualism|multilingual]], [[Multimodal learning|multimodal]] [[Large language model|large language models]] and [[generative pre-trained transformer]]. Together with the applications and implementation frameworks, the Bharat GPT Consortium intends to publish a series of [[Foundation model|foundation models]] in order to meet the needs of developers and businesses.<ref name=":8" /> The '''Bharat''' '''GPT Consortium''' was established in 2022 under the [[Public–private partnerships in India|public-private partnership]] with [[IIT Bombay]], [[Jio Platforms]], [[NASSCOM]], Seetha Mahalaxmi Healthcare, [[Bhashini#Background|Digital India Bhashini Division]] ([[Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology]]), [[IIT Madras]], [[IIT Mandi]], [[IIT Hyderabad]], [[IIT Kanpur]], [[International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad]], and [[Indian Institute of Management Indore]] as members.<ref name=":8">{{Cite news |date=2023-12-28 |title=Reliance Jio to partner with IIT-B for Bharat GPT |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/mumbai-news/reliance-jio-to-partner-with-iit-b-for-bharat-gpt-101703703960287.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240224060808/https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/mumbai-news/reliance-jio-to-partner-with-iit-b-for-bharat-gpt-101703703960287.html |archive-date=2024-02-24 |access-date=2025-02-28 |work=Hindustan Times |language=en-us}}</ref><ref name=":9">{{Cite web |date=2024-01-03 |title=Jio working on Bharat GPT with IIT-B, says Akash Ambani |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/jio-working-on-bharat-gpt-with-iit-b-says-akash-ambani-9085539/ |access-date=2025-02-28 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref>  

The Bharat GPT development team is led by Professor Ganesh Ramakrishnan of IIT Bombay as principal investigator, with support from Professor Mohan Raghavan and Professor Maunendra Sankar Desarkar of IIT Hyderabad, Professor Rohit Saluja of IIT Mandi, Professor V Kamakoti of IIT Madras, Professor Arnab Bhattacharya of IIT Kanpur, Professor Kshitij Jadhav of IIT Bombay, Professor Aditya Maheshwari of IIM Indore, and Professor Ravi Kiran of IIIT-Hyderabad.<ref name=":10" /> The text-based foundation model will be released first, followed by speech and video models. In addition to licensing commercial use, the effort has been [[Open-source artificial intelligence|open-sourcing]] a large portion of its work.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pandey |first=Mohit |date=2024-01-23 |title=BharatGPT Aims to Become Meta of Indic LLMs |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/it-services/bharatgpt-aims-to-become-meta-of-indic-llms/ |access-date=2025-02-28 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref> Bharat GPT is anticipated to be activated by [[Speech recognition|speech]] and [[gesture recognition]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 December 2023 |title=All about BharatGPT, the joint AI project of Reliance Jio & IIT Bombay |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/technology/all-about-bharatgpt-the-joint-ai-project-of-reliance-jio-iit-bombay-2829861 |access-date=2025-02-28 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en}}</ref> 

On 27 December 2023, Akash Ambani announced that Jio Platforms and IIT Bombay were collaborating on Bharat GPT program.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 December 2023 |title=Jio working on 'Bharat GPT' with IIT-Bombay; to launch OS for televisions: Akash Ambani |url=https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/business/jio-working-on-bharat-gpt-with-iit-bombay-to-launch-os-for-televisions-akash-ambani-575887/ |access-date=2025-02-28 |website=The Tribune |language=en}}</ref> Jio Platforms will assist Bharat GPT with specialized downstream telecom and retail applications by developing smaller, customized models.<ref name=":11" /> By investigating the potential of AI to foster innovation across a range of goods and services, Jio hopes to achieve its larger goal of establishing a whole ecosystem of growth through Bharat GPT.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goel |first=Yashika |date=2023-12-28 |title=India's "Bharatgpt" AI Will Be Built by Reliance Jio and IIT Bombay.. |url=https://www.businessoutreach.in/indias-bharatgpt-ai-will/ |access-date=2025-02-28 |website=Business Outreach}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Pandey |first=Surabhi |date=2023-12-28 |title=BharatGPT: Akash Ambani drops key updates on Reliance Jio-IIT Bombay's key AI project |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/life/technology-bharatgpt-akash-ambani-drops-key-updates-on-reliance-jio-iit-bombays-key-ai-project-bkg-3350016/ |access-date=2025-02-28 |website=FE Tech Bytes |language=en}}</ref> Bharat GPT Consortium is assisting in the interpretation of official documents, such as court orders, in close collaboration with the [[Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions|Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances]].<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":12" /> 

India's first [[ChatGPT]]-style service, will be launched in March 2024 by Bharat GPT Consortium, with assistance from the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]], and [[Reliance Industries]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-02-25 |title=BharatGPT Hanooman: All you need to know about the AI model developed by Reliance and 9 IITs across the country |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/gadgets-news/bharatgpt-hanooman-all-you-need-to-know-about-the-ai-model-developed-by-reliance-and-9-iits-across-the-country/articleshow/107879328.cms |access-date=2025-02-28 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> The four primary areas in which Bharat GPT sees its model operating are healthcare, financial services, governance, and education, supporting 11 [[Indian languages (India)|Indian languages]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rai |first=Saritha |date=20 February 2024 |title=AI Model Backed by Asia's Richest Person to Launch in March |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-02-21/an-ai-model-backed-by-mukesh-ambani-speeds-toward-a-march-india-rollout |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240306224444/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-02-21/an-ai-model-backed-by-mukesh-ambani-speeds-toward-a-march-india-rollout |archive-date=2024-03-06 |access-date=2025-02-27 |work=Bloomberg.com |language=en}}</ref> 

=== Hanooman series ===
Seetha Mahalaxmi Healthcare (SML) revealed the Hanooman series [[Large language model|LLM]] in February 2024 in collaboration with the Bharat GPT Consortium. Among the Hanooman series, the first four AI models—1.5 billion, 7 billion, 13 billion, and 40 billion parameters in size—will be made available as [[Open source|open-source]] after being trained on 22 Indian languages. The ability to generate text-to-text, [[Text-to-video model|text-to-video]], [[speech synthesis]] and [[speech recognition]] will be aided by Hanooman's [[multimodal learning]] capability. SML is negotiating with healthcare organizations, [[BFSI]], and mobile app developers to create customized models by refining the Hanooman series. The healthcare model VizzhyGPT is the first of these refined iterations, having been trained on extensive [[multiomics]], [[clinical research]], and [[electronic health record]] data.<ref name=":11">{{Cite news |last=Lohchab |first=Himanshi |date=2024-02-20 |title=SML in partnership with BharatGPT ecosystem unveils 'Hanooman' Indic LLMs |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/technology/bharatgpt-consortium-unveils-hanooman-a-series-of-indic-large-language-models/articleshow/107857921.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-02-27 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref> 

Hanooman's [[alpha version]], which lacks multimodal features and internet access, was launched on 10 May 2024, in 98 international languages, including 12 Indian languages ([[Hindi]], [[Marathi language|Marathi]], [[Gujarati language|Gujarati]], [[Bengali language|Bengali]], [[Kannada]], [[Odia language|Odia]], [[Punjabi language|Punjabi]], [[Assamese language|Assamese]], [[Tamil language|Tamil]], [[Telugu language|Telugu]], [[Malayalam]], and [[Sindhi language|Sindhi]]). It enables tutoring, coding, and conversation. The platform is collaborating with [[NASSCOM]], [[Hewlett-Packard]], and the [[Government of Telangana]]. [[Yotta Infrastructure]] will supply GPU cloud infrastructure. As of 14 May 2024, the Hanooman chatbot is accessible via both a [[Web client|web-client]] and an [[Android application]].<ref name=":12">{{Cite web |last=Mishra |first=Ashutosh |date=10 May 2024 |title=Indian GenAI platform Hanooman goes live in 98 global languages |url=https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/indian-genai-platform-hanooman-goes-live-in-98-global-languages-124051000962_1.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240516072238/https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/indian-genai-platform-hanooman-goes-live-in-98-global-languages-124051000962_1.html |archive-date=2024-05-16 |access-date=2025-02-27 |website=Business Standard |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-14 |title=A Bhartiya AI: Hanooman AI launched in India, works in 98 languages including 12 Indian |url=https://www.firstpost.com/tech/a-bhartiya-ai-hanooman-ai-launched-in-india-works-in-98-languages-including-12-indian-13770720.html |access-date=2025-02-27 |website=Firstpost |language=en-us}}</ref>

Hanooman is jointly owned by SML and 3AI Holding Limited, an AI [[investment company]] based in [[Abu Dhabi]]. Both businesses will own 50% share under joint ownership arrangement. In order to improve Hanooman's text, voice, image, and coding capabilities for users, it will be able to access 3AI Holding's Omega [[GenAI]], which is being created with 665 billion [[Parameter|parameters]] and 20 trillion tokens. For business clients, Hanooman will launch a [[Proprietary software|proprietary model]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gupta |first=Paromita |date=2024-04-04 |title=3AI and SML Partner to Jointly Own GenAI platform Hanooman |url=https://www.entrepreneur.com/en-in/news-and-trends/3ai-and-sml-partner-to-jointly-own-genai-platform-hanooman/472171 |access-date=2025-02-27 |website=Entrepreneur |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-04-04 |title=Abu Dhabi's 3AI, SML in pact to jointly own Indian genAI platform Hanooman |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/technology/3ai-holding-sml-in-pact-to-jointly-own-genai-platform-hanooman/articleshow/109038811.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-02-27 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref>

== BharatGen ==
BharatGen, formerly known as BharatGPT, is an Indian government-funded artificial intelligence project focused on developing India-centric [[foundation model]]s. The project was proposed by IIT Bombay professor Ganesh Ramakrishnan and is intended to support [[GenAI|generative AI]] systems that account for India's linguistic and cultural diversity. BharatGen was formally introduced on 30 September 2024 as an [[open source|open-source]], [[Multimodal learning|multimodal]] and [[Multilingualism|multilingual]] initiative. The [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]] is funding the project with an allocation of less than {{INRConvert|235|c|lk=on|year=2024}} under the National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems. The project also seeks to develop domestically controlled AI systems for applications where reliance on foreign models may raise security or data-governance concerns. Ramakrishnan had previously advocated a [[Public–private partnerships in India|public–private partnership]] for AI development through the BharatGPT programme, elements of which were subsequently incorporated into BharatGen. The project was scheduled for completion by 2026.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last=Pandey |first=Mohit |date=2024-10-02 |title=Government of India Launches BharatGen, First Government-Funded Multimodal AI Initiative |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/government-of-india-launches-bharatgen-first-government-funded-multimodal-ai-initiative/ |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Pandey |first=Mohit |date=2025-02-24 |title=This Govt-Funded ₹235 Cr AI Initiative is India's Real Answer to DeepSeek |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-features/this-govt-funded-%E2%82%B9235-cr-ai-initiative-is-indias-real-answer-to-deepseek/ |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

BharatGen is organized as a national programme involving multiple government ministries and research institutions. Its models and associated [[intellectual property]] are intended to be developed and retained in India. Computing resources for the programme are provided through the IndiaAI Compute Facility, while [[Yotta Infrastructure]] and Neysa provide [[Cloud computing|cloud computing]] support. Academic institutions and faculty members also participate in research and development under the programme.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pandey |first=Mohit |date=2025-02-24 |title=This Govt-Funded ₹235 Cr AI Initiative is India's Real Answer to DeepSeek |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-features/this-govt-funded-%E2%82%B9235-cr-ai-initiative-is-indias-real-answer-to-deepseek/ |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Pandey |first=Mohit |date=2025-01-29 |title=India Will Have its Own LLM Soon, Says IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/india-will-have-its-own-llm-soon-says-it-minister-ashwini-vaishnaw/ |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

The BharatGen consortium develops the project's models and supporting technical infrastructure. As of February 2025, it included about 50–60 researchers as well as student contributors from the [[Indian Institute of Management Indore]], the [[International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad]], [[IIT Bombay]], [[IIT Kanpur]], [[IIT Hyderabad]], [[IIT Mandi]], and [[IIT Madras]]. The consortium also includes researchers and specialists from fields including behavioral economics, engineering, artificial intelligence and design. Participating institutions work on models for [[Speech recognition|speech]], [[Language model|language]] and [[Computer vision|vision]]. The project is intended to cover languages and writing systems used in India, including languages that have relatively limited representation in existing AI training datasets.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pandit |first=Niraj |date=2024-10-04 |title=BharatGen geared to put a desi spin on ChatGPT, IIT-Bombay plays role |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/mumbai-news/bharatgen-geared-to-put-a-desi-spin-on-chatgpt-101727982824794.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241004070214/https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/mumbai-news/bharatgen-geared-to-put-a-desi-spin-on-chatgpt-101727982824794.html |archive-date=2024-10-04 |access-date=2025-02-26 |work=Hindustan Times |language=en-us}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite news |date=18 December 2024 |title=Parliament Question: Launch of BharatGen |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2085534 |access-date=26 February 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]] |agency=Ministry of Science & Technology, Government of India}}</ref>

On 30 January 2025, Minister of Electronics and Information Technology [[Ashwini Vaishnaw]] said that the framework for the AI model had been completed and that development had been underway for approximately one and a half years. According to Vaishnaw, an initial version was expected within four to ten months.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garg |first=Ankita |date=2025-01-30 |title=India to develop its own AI model like ChatGPT and DeepSeek in 10 months: Ashwini Vaishnaw |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/technology/news/story/india-to-develop-its-own-ai-model-like-chatgpt-and-deepseek-in-10-months-ashwini-vaishnaw-2672368-2025-01-30 |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=India Today |language=en}}</ref>

BharatGen also established the [[Bharat Data Sagar]] initiative, a multilingual data repository for AI research. The repository is intended to collect data for Indian languages that are underrepresented in existing [[Data corpus|corpora]], including material reflecting regional languages, dialects and cultural contexts. Data from the initiative is intended for use in training and adapting language and multimodal models. BharatGen also develops tools for translation and for generating content in regional languages and dialects.<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":6" />

In October 2024, BharatGen launched e-vikrAI, an e-commerce application based on [[Computer vision|vision-language models]]. The system generates product catalogue information from images supplied by sellers, including titles, descriptions, product features and suggested prices. It can also translate product descriptions into Indian languages and provide spoken versions of the generated text.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pandey |first=Mohit |date=2024-10-16 |title=BharatGen Launches e-vikrAI, Vision Language Model for Indic e-Commerce |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/bharatgen-launches-e-vikrai-vision-language-model-for-indic-e-commerce/ |access-date=2025-02-27 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2024-10-25 |title=Two Hyderabad research institutes lead country's AI revolution with BharatGen's e-VikrAI |url=https://www.deccanchronicle.com/southern-states/telangana/two-hyderabad-research-institutes-lead-countrys-ai-revolution-with-bharatgens-e-vikrai-1833071 |access-date=2025-02-27 |website=deccanchronicle.com |language=en}}</ref>

Additionally, IndiaAI Overheads and Contingency received funding of {{INRConvert|102.69|c|lk=on}}.<ref>{{Cite web |last=K |first=Sakshi Sadashiv |date=2024-12-05 |title=IndiaAI Mission: Rs. 10,372 Cr Budget Breakdown Revealed |url=https://www.medianama.com/2024/12/223-indiaai-mission-expenditure-budget/ |access-date=2025-06-04 |website=MEDIANAMA |language=en-US}}</ref> The [[digital public infrastructure]] framework for AI in India guarantees consent-based, ethically generated datasets while lowering dependency on foreign and [[synthetic data]].<ref name=":14">{{Cite news |date=6 March 2025 |title=Ashwini Vaishnaw unveils India AI compute portal, AIKosha and other AI initiatives on IndiaAI Mission anniversary to enable India's AI research and innovation ecosystem |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2108961 |access-date=4 June 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]] |agency=Ministry of Electronics & IT, Government of India.}}</ref> 

On 30 January 2025, [[Ashwini Vaishnaw]], the [[Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology|Minister for Electronics and information Technology]], confirmed that the IndiaAI Mission would customize native AI solutions for the Indian context using [[Indian languages (India)|Indian languages]], supported by a state-of-the-art shared computing infrastructure. The initial AI model starts with a compute capacity of about 10,000 [[GPUs]], with the remaining 8693 GPUs to be added shortly. The facility includes 7,200 [[AMD Instinct#Products|AMD Instinct MI200]] and [[AMD Instinct#Products|MI300 series]], 12,896 [[Hopper (microarchitecture)#H100 accelerator and DGX H100|Nvidia H100]], and 1,480 [[Hopper (microarchitecture)#H100 accelerator and DGX H100|H200]] processors. The cost of computing the AI model will be less than [[₹]]100 per hour following a 40% government subsidy, with half-yearly and annual plans for developers, researchers, and students.<ref name=":5">{{Cite news |date=30 January 2025 |title=With robust and high end Common computing facility in place, India all set to launch its own safe & secure indigenous AI model at affordable cost soon: Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2097709 |access-date=24 February 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]] |agency=Ministry of Electronics & IT, Government of India}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sur |first=Aihik |date=22 January 2025 |title=IndiaAI Mission selects 10 firms to bid for 10,000 GPU mega tender |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/technology/indiaai-mission-selects-10-firms-to-bid-for-10-000-gpu-mega-tender-article-12916413.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250129013128/https://www.moneycontrol.com/technology/indiaai-mission-selects-10-firms-to-bid-for-10-000-gpu-mega-tender-article-12916413.html |archive-date=2025-01-29 |access-date=2025-02-24 |website=Moneycontrol |language=en-US}}</ref> 

Startups, MSMEs, universities, researchers, students, and governmental organizations will all be able to access AI compute, network, storage, platform, and cloud services through the IndiaAI Compute Portal. Easy access to Nvidia H100, H200, [[A100 GPU|A100]], [[List of Nvidia graphics processing units#Tesla|L40S]], and [[List of Nvidia graphics processing units#Tesla|L4]], [[AMD Instinct#MI300 series|AMD MI300x]] and [[AMD Instinct#Products|325X]], [[Intel#'IDM 2.0' strategy|Intel Gaudi 2]], [[AWS Trainium]], and [[Inferentia]] will be made possible by the portal. Nearly 45% of the IndiaAI Mission's budget goes into the AI Compute Portal.<ref name=":14" /> 

Accessing more expensive GPUs would cost ₹150 per hour, while utilizing less expensive GPUs would cost ₹115.85 per hour. Orient Technologies, CMS Computers Limited, SHI Locuz, CtrlS, NxtGen Cloud Technologies, [[Yotta Infrastructure]], [[Jio Platforms]], [[Tata Communications]], E2E Networks, and Vensysco Technologies have been approved by the government to provide 18,693 GPUs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barik |first=Soumyarendra |date=2025-01-31 |title=India braces up for AI challenge, plans own LLM foundational model to rival ChatGPT, DeepSeek R1 |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/business/india-world-class-ai-model-ashwini-vaishnaw-9807337/ |access-date=2025-02-27 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref>

As part of the IndianAI Mission, the [[union government]], in April 2025, selected [[Sarvam AI]], to develop the country's first sovereign [[LLM]], which will include the capabilities of reasoning, voice, and fluency in Indian languages.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 April 2025 |title=Sarvam AI to build India's first sovereign LLM with reasoning and voice capabilities |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/technology/artificial-intelligence/sarvam-ai-to-build-indias-first-sovereign-llm-with-reasoning-and-voice-capabilities-9967108/ |access-date=20 May 2025 |website=The Indian Express}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=28 April 2025 |title=India selects Sarvam to build sovereign AI model under IndiaAI mission - BusinessToday |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/tech-today/news/story/india-selects-sarvam-to-build-sovereign-ai-model-under-indiaai-mission-473791-2025-04-28 |access-date=20 May 2025 |website=Business Today}}</ref> As of May 2025, the government, as part of the IndianAI Mission, is supporting Indian researchers in designing indigenous GPUs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chintapali |first=Rohit |date=3 May 2025 |title=Spotlight: IndiaAI Mission |url=https://www.businessworld.in/article/spotlight-indiaai-mission-555677 |access-date=20 May 2025 |website=BW Businessworld}}</ref>

Ashwini Vaishnaw announced AIKosha: IndiaAI Datasets Platform, the AI Compute Portal, the AI Competency Framework for Public Sector Officials, iGOT-AI Mission Karmayogi, the IndiaAI Startups Global Acceleration Program with [[Station F]], the IndiaAI Application Development Initiative, and IndiaAI FutureSkills on 6 March 2025, as part of the IndiaAI Mission to strengthen AI-driven research, innovation, and skill development. For public officials, the iGOT-AI Mission Karmayogi incorporates AI-driven learning recommendations. 

'''AIKosha: IndiaAI Datasets Platform'''

To facilitate AI innovation, AIKosha will offer a safe, centralized platform with easy access to a database of models, use cases, and datasets. Through an integrated development environment, tools, and tutorials, it offers AI [[Sandbox (software development)|sandbox]] capabilities. AIKosha has features like permission-based access, content discoverability, AI readiness scoring of datasets, and security methods including secure [[API|APIs]], [[Firewall (computing)|firewalls]] for real-time harmful traffic filtering, and [[data encryption]] both in motion and at rest. More than 80 models and 300 datasets are available on AIKosha.<ref name=":14" /> Both the public and private sector organizations gather AIKosha datasets, which include [[Census of India|census data]], [[geospatial data]], and [[Linguistics|linguistic]] data.<ref name=":15">{{Cite web |last=Parasnis |first=Sharveya |date=2025-03-07 |title=IndiaAI Mission: MeitY Launches New AI Initiatives |url=https://www.medianama.com/2025/03/223-meity-ai-driven-initiatives-indiaai-mission-ashwini-vaishnaw/ |access-date=2025-06-04 |website=MEDIANAMA |language=en-US}}</ref> 

'''IndiaAI Startups Global Acceleration Program'''

The IndiaAI Mission will begin a four-month acceleration program in partnership with [[Station F]] and [[HEC Paris]] from 2025. The ten shortlisted AI [[startup companies]] will have access to networking opportunities, mentorship, and international market expansion in [[Europe]].<ref name=":14" />

=== AI Research Analytics and Knowledge Dissemination Platform ===
With a peak performance of 13,170 [[teraflops]], AIRAWAT-PSAI is the biggest and fastest AI supercomputing machine in India. It was deployed at [[C-DAC|C-DAC, Pune]] in 2023 and is maintained by Netweb Technologies.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-08-17 |title=India's AI supercomputer 'AIRAWAT' makes it to the list of world's '100 most powerful' |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/gadgets-news/indias-ai-supercomputer-airawat-makes-it-to-the-list-of-worlds-100-most-powerful/articleshow/100487763.cms |access-date=2025-06-04 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> 

[[MeitY]] is also funding the implementation of 200 AI [[Petaflops]] [[Mixed-precision arithmetic|Mixed Precision]] peak computing capacity (scalable to 790 AI Petaflops) [[Proof of concept|Proof of Concept]] for AI Research Analytics and Knowledge Dissemination Platform (AIRAWAT), which is being carried out by C-DAC, Pune. A combined peak compute of 410 AI Petaflops Mixed Precision and a sustained compute capability of 8.5 Petaflops ([[Rmax (computing)|Rmax]]) [[Double-precision floating-point format|Double Precision]] are achieved by combining the 200 AI Petaflop AIRAWAT PoC with the 210 AI Petaflop [[PARAM Siddhi-AI]]. 13 Petaflops is the maximum computation capacity (Double Precision, Rpeak). A plan for expanding AIRAWAT to 1,000 AI Petaflops of Mixed Precision computing capacity has been envisioned by MeitY. With its extensive, power-optimized AI cloud infrastructure, AIRAWAT will serve as a common computational cloud platform for Big Data Analytics and Assimilation, linking all Centers for Research Excellence in Artificial Intelligence (COREs), Indian Centres for Transformational AI (ICTAIs), and other academic, research lab, scientific community, industry, and start-up institutions with the National Knowledge Network.

With an emphasis on [[NLP (computer science)|NLP]], surveillance and [[image processing]], [[pattern recognition]], [[medical imaging]], education, agriculture, finance, healthcare, audio assistance, robotics, national security, defense, the automotive industry, supply chain management, [[human resource development]], and anomalous behavior detection from [[video analytics]], AIRAWAT will support the field of applied AI. Deployed under the [[National Supercomputing Mission]], it will support the [[Digital India]] [[Bhashini]] initiative and accomplish the goals of the National Program on AI.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AIRAWAT-PSAI |url=https://airawat.cdac.in/airawat/ |access-date=4 June 2025 |website=Centre for Development of Advanced Computing}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=24 May 2023 |title=AI Supercomputer 'AIRAWAT' puts India among top supercomputing league |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1926942 |access-date=4 June 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]] |agency=Ministry of Electronics & IT, Government of India.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=27 December 2024 |title=Year End Review 2024 of Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology Part-1 |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2088268 |access-date=4 June 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]] |agency=Ministry of Electronics & IT, Government of India.}}</ref>  

== International collaboration ==
[[Prime Minister of India|Prime Minister]] [[Narendra Modi]] with [[NITI Aayog]] officially opened the [[World Economic Forum]]'s Center for the Fourth Industrial Revolution liaison office in [[Navi Mumbai]] on 11 October 2018.<ref>{{Cite news |date=11 October 2018 |title=PM addresses event to mark launch of the Centre for the Fourth Industrial Revolution |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1549430 |access-date=6 June 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]] |agency=Prime Minister's Office, Government of India.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=C4IR India |url=https://centres.weforum.org/centre-for-the-fourth-industrial-revolution/india |access-date=2025-06-06 |website=centres.weforum.org |language=en}}</ref> Its objective is to foster the responsible adoption and deployment of new technologies by designing policy frameworks and protocols with the government, corporations, academic institutions, [[startups]], and international organizations. The Indian team will collaborate with their counterparts in [[Beijing]], [[Tokyo]], and [[San Francisco]] to focus on [[blockchain]] & [[Distributed ledger|DLT]], AI & [[Machine learning|ML]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2018-10-11 |title=WEF launches Centre for Fourth Industrial Revolution in India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/wef-launches-centre-for-fourth-industrial-revolution-in-india/articleshow/66166216.cms |access-date=2025-06-06 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> To increase farmers' incomes, [[World Economic Forum#Organization|C4IR]] has been working on AI-driven agricultural initiatives since 2018. In January 2024, C4IR, [[MeitY]], [[NASSCOM]], and the [[Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India|Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser]] launched the '''AI for India 2030 initiative'''. Its goal is to offer a systematic approach to the ethical, inclusive, and responsible adoption of AI in India.<ref>{{Cite news |last= |date=2025-01-20 |title=India at forefront of age defined by tech evolution: WEF report |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/Economy/india-at-forefront-of-age-defined-by-tech-evolution-wef-report/article69119315.ece |access-date=2025-06-06 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Kaushik |first1=Purushottam |last2=Sharma |first2=Harsh |last3=Sarna |first3=Ayushi |date=22 January 2025 |title=AI for India 2030: A blueprint for inclusive growth and global leadership |url=https://www.weforum.org/stories/2025/01/ai-for-india-2030-blueprint-inclusive-growth-global-leadership/ |access-date=6 June 2025 |website=World Economic Forum}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Centre for the Fourth Industrial Revolution (C4IR) India – an Impact Journey |url=https://reports.weforum.org/docs/WEF_C4IR_India_An_Impact_Journey_2025.pdf |access-date=6 June 2025 |website=World Economic Forum}}</ref>

India's [[Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology]] and Japan's [[Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry|Ministry of Economy, Trade, and Industry]] signed a memorandum of cooperation on 29 October 2018, which outlines the two nations' cooperation in AI and [[IoT]] as part of '''India-Japan Cooperation on Digital Partnership'''. In an effort to strengthen ties between NITI Aayog and [[Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry|METI]], India and Japan signed a broad statement of intent on AI under "Society 5.0" that included the exploration of potential institutional collaborations, such as joint projects between [[IIT Hyderabad]] and Artificial Intelligence Research Centre ([[National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology]]), related to [[machine learning]], [[deep learning]], [[data mining]], and other AI themes. Joint scientific and technological cooperation in [[Machine learning|ML]], and [[probabilistic logic]] techniques for various data types and combinations were added to the extended MoU on 24 December 2021.<ref>{{Cite news |date=29 October 2018 |title=India-Japan Fact Sheets. India-Japan Development Cooperation in the Indo-Pacific, including Africa |url=https://pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=184461 |access-date=1 March 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau ]] |agency=Prime Minister's Office, Government of India}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2021-12-24 |title=Japanese research institute, IIT-H renew MoU |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/japanese-research-institute-iit-h-renew-mou/article38030467.ece |access-date=2025-03-01 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

It will also facilitate AI innovation, exchange ideas for building an AI workforce, and suggest ways to promote collaborations.<ref>{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2021-03-18 |title=India, US launch AI-focused forum to scale up science & technology relationship |url=https://www.livemint.com/science/news/india-us-launch-ai-focused-forum-to-scale-up-science-technology-relationship-11616072222839.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210322010058/https://www.livemint.com/science/news/india-us-launch-ai-focused-forum-to-scale-up-science-technology-relationship-11616072222839.html |archive-date=2021-03-22 |access-date=2025-02-08 |work=mint |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-03-28 |title=US-India Artificial Intelligence Initiative |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/business-tech/us-india-artificial-intelligence-initiative/article34183767.ece |access-date=2025-02-08 |website=BusinessLine |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tandon |first=Tulika |date=2023-07-01 |title=All about US India Artificial Intelligence Initiative (USIAI) |url=https://www.jagranjosh.com/general-knowledge/all-about-us-india-artificial-intelligence-initiative-usiai-1616403169-1 |access-date=2025-02-08 |website=Jagranjosh.com |language=en}}</ref>

The [[United States]] and India expanded their joint cyber training and exercises in 2022 and initiated the '''Defense Artificial Intelligence Dialogue'''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Readout of the Inaugural U.S. – India Advanced Domains Defense Dialogue |url=https://www.war.gov/News/Releases/Release/Article/3408336/readout-of-the-inaugural-us-india-advanced-domains-defense-dialogue/ |access-date=2025-01-23 |website=U.S. Department of Defense |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Si-soo |first=Park |date=2022-04-12 |title=US, India agree to cooperate on space situational awareness |url=https://spacenews.com/us-india-agree-to-cooperate-on-space-situational-awareness/ |access-date=2025-01-23 |website=SpaceNews |language=en-US}}</ref> According to [[Cleo Paskal]], a non-resident senior fellow at the [[Foundation for Defense of Democracies]], the Indian community has influenced AI research and development in the US for many years. Things are taken to the next level by the Defense Artificial Intelligence Dialogue.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Demarest |first=Colin |date=2022-04-18 |title=US and India launch talks about military AI |url=https://www.c4isrnet.com/artificial-intelligence/2022/04/15/us-and-india-launch-talks-about-military-ai/ |access-date=2025-01-23 |website=C4ISRNet |language=en}}</ref> In the same year, the US intends to join six of India's Technology Innovation Hubs to support collaborative research projects in fields including AI, advanced wireless technologies, and data science to further advancements in applications like agriculture, health, and climate. == Impact ==

=== Agriculture ===
On 12 December 2023, KissanAI announced the release of Dhenu 1.0, world's first agriculture-specific [[Large language model|LLM]] designed for Indian farmers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Verma |first=Shreshtha |date=23 December 2023 |title=What is KissanAI? Explore The Startup Streamlining Farmers' Lives! |url=https://www.tice.news/tice-trending/kissanai-chatgpt-see-how-this-startup-is-simplifying-farmer-everyday-life-2049132 |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=tice.news |language=en}}</ref> It can handle 300,000 instruction sets and understand English, [[Hindi]], and [[Hinglish]] queries. The platform provides voice-based, tailored assistance. KissanAI used Sarvam AI's OpenHathi for [[bilingual]] support and worked with NimbleBox for [[API|APIs]]. Dhenu 1.0 utilizes OpenHermes 2.5 [[Mistral AI#Models|Mistral 7B]]. KissanAI is supported by [[Microsoft for Startups]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Upadhyay |first=Shyam Nandan |date=2023-12-12 |title=KissanAI Unveils Dhenu 1.0 LLM for India's Agricultural Challenges |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/deep-tech/kissanai-unveils-dhenu-1-0-llm-for-indias-agricultural-challenges/ |access-date=2025-02-25 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jindal |first=Siddharth |date=2023-12-25 |title=How Pratik Desai is Sowing AI Seeds in India |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-features/how-pratik-desai-is-sowing-ai-seeds-in-india/ |access-date=2025-02-25 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref> For climate resilient agriculture practices, KissanAI partnered with the [[United Nations Development Programme]] in January 2024 to develop a voice-based [[vernacular]] [[GenAI]] virtual assistant. The main goals of this project are to overcome language barriers and offer easily comprehensible information so that female farmers can actively engage in and profit from generative AI developments.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jindal |first=Siddharth |date=2024-01-05 |title=KissanAI Partners with UNDP to Launch CoPilot for Farmers |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/kissanai-partners-with-undp-to-launch-copilot-for-farmers/ |access-date=2025-02-25 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Upadhyay |first=Shyam Nandan |date=2024-06-08 |title=KissanAI accepted for NVIDIA Inception Program |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/kissanai-accepted-for-nvidia-inception-program/ |access-date=2025-02-25 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref> Dhenu2, an [[Open source|open-source]] version, was launched in October 2024, providing solutions for agribusinesses, farmers, and policymakers worldwide. It is available in three models: 8B, 3B, and 1B, and is powered by the [[Llama 3]]. The platform is based on 1.5 million synthetic and real-world instructions that cover more than 4,000 agricultural topics and categories. Over 100,000 farmers were interviewed to gain insights that provided practical information for better decision-making.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jindal |first=Siddharth |date=2024-10-24 |title=KissanAI Launches Dhenu2 AI to Empower Farmers with Real-World Insights |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/kissanai-launches-dhenu2-ai-to-empower-farmers-with-real-world-insights/ |access-date=2025-02-25 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref> 

Uttar Pradesh Open Network for Agriculture, a [[digital public infrastructure]], powered by [[Gemini (language model)|Gemini]] and [[Open Network for Digital Commerce#Beckn Protocol|Beckn protocol]], was launched in January 2025 by the [[Government of Uttar Pradesh]] in collaboration with [[Google Cloud Platform]]. Farmers will get one-stop access to market linkages, loans, mechanization, and advisory services for selling their produce. [[Voice user interface]] will be available to farmers in Hindi, [[Bengali language|Bengali]], [[Telugu language|Telugu]], [[Kannada]], [[Gujarati language|Gujarati]], and [[Punjabi language|Punjabi]], with other [[Indian languages (India)|Indian languages]] to be added in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=8 January 2025 |title=UP govt, Google Cloud sign MOU for launch of Gemini-powered, Beckn-enabled open network for agriculture |url=https://government.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/digital-india/up-govt-google-cloud-sign-mou-for-launch-of-gemini-powered-beckn-enabled-open-network-for-agriculture/117053955 |access-date=2025-02-25 |website=ETGovernment.com |language=en}}</ref>

IIT Indore established on 27 January 2025 AgriHub, a center of excellence for sustainable agriculture co-funded by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and the Government of Madhya Pradesh. The center uses Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Deep Learning technologies for agricultural research. The major areas of research include big data analysis, genomics research, precision agriculture, xerophytes and AI-based disease diagnostics <ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-01-28 |title=IIT-I unveils AI-driven Centre of Excellence for sustainable agri |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/indore/iit-i-unveils-ai-driven-centre-of-excellence-for-sustainable-agri/articleshow/117612188.cms |access-date=2025-02-25 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

Farmers in [[Fazilka district|Fazilka]] have embraced AI-powered weather sensors created by [[IIT Ropar]]. It provides real-time information on atmospheric conditions by utilizing data gathered from satellites, weather balloons and a network of weather stations on the ground. Parameters like temperature, humidity, precipitation, and lux are used with data from the [[India Meteorological Department]] to forecast rainfall.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mohan |first=Vibhor |date=2025-01-29 |title=Kinnow farmers adopt AI-powered weather stations to mitigate risks |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/chandigarh/kinnow-farmers-adopt-ai-powered-weather-stations-to-mitigate-risks/articleshow/117652011.cms |access-date=2025-02-25 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

AI is being used by the [[Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare]] to assist farmers. An AI-powered chatbot called Kisan e-Mitra was built to help farmers with their questions on [[Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi]] scheme in multiple Indian languages. The [[National Pest Surveillance System]] uses AI and [[Machine learning|ML]] to identify pest infestation, allowing for prompt action for healthier crops and addressing the loss of produce brought on by climate change. AI-based analytics that use field photos to monitor and evaluate crop health utilizing weather, soil moisture, and satellite data for [[wheat]] and [[rice]] cultivation.<ref>{{Cite news |date=7 February 2025 |title=Use of AI in agriculture |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2100755 |access-date=25 February 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]] |agency=Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India}}</ref>

The use of AI in Khutbav village by the Agriculture Development Trust and [[Microsoft]] in 2025 led to a 40% increase in yield and a 50% reduction in production costs due to water and pesticide usage. Through a smartphone application Agripilot.ai developed by Click2Cloud, the AI notify farmers of possible pest attacks, soil conditions, air speed, and weather conditions to determine when to apply pesticides and how much water the crop requires. Utilizing a variety of data sources, including [[satellite imagery]], [[weather forecasts]], soil sensors, and inputs unique to each farm, the AI generate personalized suggestions for farmers. Microsoft's Azure Data Manager for Agriculture (formerly Microsoft FarmBeats), is used to process this data. The annual fee for AI services is ₹10,000.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Khairnar |first=Abhay |date=11 February 2025 |title=How AI is revolutionising sugarcane farming in Maha |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/pune-news/how-ai-is-revolutionising-sugarcane-farming-in-maha-101739214058733.html |access-date=25 February 2025 |work=[[Hindustan Times]]}}</ref> In order to offer insights, the data is analyzed by the open-source research project FarmVibes.ai in conjunction with historical crop data. For the farmer, [[Microsoft Azure]] [[OpenAI]] Service transforms these details into easy-to-follow steps.<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 January 2025 |title='Farm Of The Future': How AI Is Helping Sugarcane Farmers In Maharashtra |url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/farm-of-the-future-how-ai-is-helping-sugarcane-farmers-in-maharashtra-7419774 |access-date=2025-02-25 |website=ndtv.com |language=en}}</ref>

In 100 villages, the [[Assam Government|Assam government]] will support the establishment of AI-powered agri-hubs, where drones and AI would assist farmers in making data-driven decisions, increasing yields, and promoting sustainability, according to the state budget for 2025–2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 March 2025 |title=Assam mulls India's first AI lab for cyber surveillance |url=https://www.theweek.in/wire-updates/business/2025/03/10/cal48-as-budget-ai.html |access-date=2025-03-15 |website=The Week |language=en}}</ref>
