=== Internal security ===
To dismantle [[Organised crime in India|organized crime]] and [[Terrorism in India|terrorism]] networks, [[Ministry of Home Affairs (India)|Ministry of Home Affairs]] established [[NATGRID#Organised Crime Network Database|Organised Crime Network Database]] on 26 December 2025. The database was launched by [[Union Home Minister]] [[Amit Shah]] at Anti-Terror Conference in Delhi. Investigative agencies can utilize the OCND, an AI-powered advanced analytics tool to rapidly gather comprehensive information about terrorist networks and [[crime syndicates]]. Investigating agencies can instantly access [[First information report|first information reports]], [[Chargesheet|chargesheets]], dossiers, and other vital information about crimes from all [[Indian states]]. To create the OCND, the [[National Investigation Agency]] collaborated closely with state police agencies and [[NATGRID]]. OCND functions like [[ChatGPT]] and offers voice matching and fingerprint data in addition to profile data.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-12-26 |title='Functions like ChatGPT': AI-powered Organised Crime Network Database launched; provides FIRs and dossiers in real time |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/functions-like-chatgpt-ai-powered-organised-crime-network-database-launched-provides-firs-and-dossiers-to-agencies-in-real-time/articleshow/126187643.cms |access-date=2025-12-29 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-12-27 |title=AI-powered Organised Crime Network Database (OCND) launches in India with ChatGPT-like functionality |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/life/technology-ai-powered-organised-crime-network-database-ocnd-launches-in-india-with-chatgpt-like-functionality-4090196/ |access-date=2025-12-29 |website=FE Tech Bytes |language=en}}</ref>

=== Space ===
MOI-TD, India's first AI lab in space, is being built by TakeMe2Space. AI's potential utility in space will be demonstrated with the MOI-TD mission. In order to foresee natural disasters and comprehend climate change, the MOI-TD will assist with environmental monitoring, weather pattern analysis, and Earth's surface change tracking. The lab will process the data in real time, allowing for analysis of the information at the time of collection.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reddy |first=Anurag |date=2025-02-11 |title=Hyderabad Startup Building India's First AI Lab in Orbit |url=https://www.analyticsinsight.net/artificial-intelligence/hyderabad-startup-building-indias-first-ai-lab-in-orbit |access-date=2025-03-15 |website=Analytics Insight |language=en}}</ref> The MOI-TD mission showed that it was possible to run external code on the satellite, securely downlink encrypted data, and uplink huge AI models from a ground station through OrbitLab, a web-based console. It effectively validated key subsystems, including computer infrastructure (Zero Cube AI Accelerator, [[PSLV Orbital Experiment Module|POEM]] Adapter Board), actuators (MagnetoTorquers, AirTorquers, [[Reaction wheel|Reaction Wheel]]), and sensors ([[Sun sensor|Sun Sensor]], Horizon Sensor, Solar Cell, [[Inertial measurement unit|IMUs]]). The foundation for space-based computing is laid by MOI-TD. The creation of space-based data centers will be facilitated by the upcoming MOI-1 AI Lab mission. Support for the project came from the [[Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre|Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Center]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-05 |title=TakeMe2Space secures Rs 5.5 crore in Pre-Seed Funding to launch India's first AI lab in space |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/start-ups-takeme2space-secures-rs-5-5-crore-in-pre-seed-funding-to-launch-indias-first-ai-lab-in-space-3767831/ |access-date=2025-03-15 |website=Financialexpress |language=en}}</ref> One study by the [[University of Southampton]] on TakeMe2Space's AI lab used a low-power AI system to lessen [[Motion blur (media)|motion blur]] in satellite imagery.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gupta |first=Sanjana |date=2025-02-08 |title=This Hyderabad Startup is Building India's First AI Lab in Orbit |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/deep-tech/this-hyderabad-startup-is-building-indias-first-ai-lab-in-orbit/ |access-date=2025-03-16 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Healthcare ===
During the [[COVID-19 pandemic in India|COVID-19 pandemic]], Qure.ai's AI chest X-ray reporting tool, qXR, was used to identify patients for high, medium, or low risk so that [[RT-PCR]] testing could be performed. It can identify [[pulmonary consolidation]], [[ground-glass opacity]], and other signs of [[COVID-19]]. The tool provides measurements like the proportion of lung size and volume impacted by the anomalies.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bora |first=Garima |date=2020-04-30 |title=Qure.ai can detect Covid-19 lung infections in less than a minute, help triage patients |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/small-biz/startups/newsbuzz/qure-ai-can-detect-covid-19-lung-infections-in-less-than-a-minute-help-triage-patients/articleshow/75464679.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-02-08 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=6 July 2022 |title=AI, ML making equitable, high-quality healthcare a reality: Qure.ai |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/technology/ai-ml-making-equitable-high-quality-healthcare-a-reality-qure-ai-122070600388_1.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250123160438/https://www.business-standard.com/article/technology/ai-ml-making-equitable-high-quality-healthcare-a-reality-qure-ai-122070600388_1.html |archive-date=2025-01-23 |access-date=2025-02-08 |website=Business Standard |language=en-US}}</ref> The Computational and Data Sciences Collaborative Laboratory of Artificial Intelligence in Medical and Healthcare Imaging was established by [[Wipro]] [[GE HealthCare]] at [[IISc]] in September 2020. Its goal is to develop advanced diagnostic and medical image-reconstruction techniques and protocols for quicker and better imaging by utilizing deep learning, AI, and future-ready digital interfaces.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 September 2024 |title=Wipro GE Healthcare, IISc set up health tech innovation lab |url=https://www.biospectrumindia.com/news/98/17265/wipro-ge-healthcare-iisc-set-up-health-tech-innovation-lab.html |access-date=2025-02-23 |website=BioSpectrum |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Goled |first=Shraddha |date=2020-09-24 |title=Wipro GE Healthcare Collaborates With IISc To Set Up AI Healthcare Innovation Lab |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/wipro-ge-healthcare-collaborates-with-iisc-to-set-up-ai-healthcare-innovation-lab/ |access-date=2025-02-23 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

With an emphasis on neurological disease diagnosis and population-level clinical impact analysis, [[Siemens Healthineers]] established the Computational Data Sciences Collaborative Laboratory for AI in Precision Medicine at [[IISc]] in 2024 to create [[Open source|open-source]] AI tools to automate the segmentation of pathological findings in neuroimaging data.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pilla |first=Viswanath |date=2024-01-24 |title=Siemens Healthineers, IISc opens AI lab for precision medicine |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/healthcare/biotech/pharmaceuticals/siemens-healthineers-iisc-opens-ai-lab-for-precision-medicine/articleshow/107114377.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-02-23 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref> 

As part of the Interdisciplinary Group for Advanced Research on Birth Outcomes – DBT India Initiative (GARBH-Ini) program, [[IIT Madras]] and [[Translational Health Science and Technology Institute]] in 2024 created India's first AI model, Garbhini-GA2, which will accurately estimate the age of the [[fetus]] in [[pregnant women]] in the [[Second trimester|second]] and [[Third trimester|third trimesters]]. In contrast to the current methods of determining a fetus's age in India, which use the Hadlock model developed using pregnancy data from Western countries or the more recent INTERGROWTH-21st model, the Garbhini-GA2, which is specific to the Indian population, uses genetic algorithm-based methods for estimating [[gestational age]]. This model reduces the error by nearly three times. The study was carried out in collaboration with [[Pondicherry Institute of Medical Sciences]], [[Christian Medical College Vellore]], [[Safdarjung Hospital]], and Gurugram Civil Hospital. Following the completion of pan-India validation, Garbhini-GA2 will be implemented in clinics throughout the country.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 February 2024 |title=IIT-M & THSTI develop first India-specific AI model to determine foetus age |url=https://www.biospectrumindia.com/news/91/24243/iit-m-thsti-develop-first-india-specific-ai-model-to-determine-foetus-age.html |access-date=2025-02-07 |website=BioSpectrum |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sivapriyan |first=ETB |date=26 February 2024 |title=IIT Madras researchers develop first India-specific AI model to determine age of foetus |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/science/iit-madras-researchers-develop-first-india-specific-ai-model-to-determine-age-of-foetus-2910363 |access-date=2025-02-07 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en}}</ref> The [[Ministry of Science and Technology (India)|Ministry of Science and Technology]]'s [[Department of Biotechnology]] provided financing for the research, with additional support from the Robert Bosch Centre for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (IIT Madras) and the Centre for Integrative Biology and Systems Medicine (IIT Madras).<ref>{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2024-02-26 |title=India-specific model to give accurate gestational age of foetus |url=https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/science/india-specific-model-to-give-accurate-gestational-age-of-foetus/article67888396.ece |access-date=2025-02-07 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-26 |title=IIT Madras, THSTI researchers develop first India-specific AI model for foetus age |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/education-today/news/story/iit-madras-thsti-researchers-develop-first-india-specific-ai-model-for-foetus-age-2507157-2024-02-26 |access-date=2025-02-07 |website=India Today |language=en}}</ref>

In order to support healthy aging, constructive lifestyle modifications, and psycho-social wellbeing, Wipro and the Centre for Brain Research at IISc partnered in May 2024 to create an AI-based personal care engine that will consider a person's past medical history, desired health state, and behavioral responses to offer personalized help with chronic disease prevention and treatment.<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 May 2024 |title=Wipro collaborates with Centre for Brain Research at IISc for AI-driven health behaviour innovations |url=https://www.biospectrumindia.com/news/100/24690/wipro-collaborates-with-centre-for-brain-research-at-iisc-for-ai-driven-health-behaviour-innovations.html |access-date=2025-02-23 |website=BioSpectrum |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-05-28 |title=Wipro teams up with Centre for Brain Research at IISc on AI-driven health behaviour innovations |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/information-tech/wipro-teams-up-with-centre-for-brain-research-at-iisc-on-ai-driven-health-behaviour-innovations/articleshow/110486795.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-02-23 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref> Researchers from [[St. John's Medical College|St. John's Hospital]] and [[IIIT-B]] are focusing on using [[computer vision]] for early detection of [[autism]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=T.R |first=Jahnavi |date=2024-11-21 |title=Researchers use computer vision for early detection of autism |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/bangalore/researchers-use-computer-vision-for-early-detection-of-autism/article68894133.ece |access-date=2025-02-19 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

=== Mobility ===
In an effort to improve road safety and decrease fatalities by half, [[Minister of Road Transport and Highways]] [[Nitin Gadkari]] inaugurated Intelligent Solutions for Road Safety through Technology and Engineering (iRASTE) under Mission Zero on 11 September 2021. The pilot project will run for two years in [[Nagpur]]. [[Intel]], [[International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad]], [[Central Road Research Institute]], [[Mahindra & Mahindra]], and [[Nagpur Municipal Corporation]] are part of the pilot project. It is focusing on vehicle safety, mobility analysis, and infrastructure safety.<ref>{{Cite web |title=iRASTE |url=https://inai.iiit.ac.in/iraste-telangana.html |access-date=2025-02-07 |website=inai.iiit.ac.in}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gandharv |first=kumar |date=2021-09-13 |title=Nitin Gadkari Launches AI-Powered iRASTE Project For Road Safety |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/nitin-gadkari-launches-ai-powered-iraste-project-for-road-safety/ |access-date=2025-02-18 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

To improve vehicle safety, [[Nagpur Municipal Corporation|NMC]] will outfit its fleet of vehicles with [[Advanced driver-assistance system|advanced driver-assistance systems]] and [[Collision avoidance system|collision avoidance systems]]. They will also be equipped with sensors which will continuously monitor the road network's dynamic risks for mobility analysis, mapping the city into three zones: white (normal), grey (accident could happen), and black (accident has already happened). The data will be gathered by Intel AI Center at [[IIIT-H]] for monitoring and fixing the grey and black zones.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Deshpande |first=Vivek |date=2021-09-11 |title=With aim to enhance road safety in Nagpur, Nitin Gadkari launches iRASTE initiative |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/india/with-aim-to-enhance-road-safety-in-nagpur-nitin-gadkari-launches-iraste-initiative-7501907/ |access-date=2025-02-07 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=iRASTE project aims reducing road accidents, finding factors responsible: Intel India head |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/business/iraste-project-aims-reducing-road-accidents-finding-factors-responsible-intel-india-head-1029918.html |access-date=2025-02-07 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en}}</ref>

MINRO at IIIT-B is working on traffic analysis of Indian road conditions, analyzing traffic data, and using data for multimodal transport to make recommendations about the locations of  [[Urban rail transit in India|rail transit]] and [[Bus station|bus stations]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Kannaiah |first=Venkatesh |date=2024-03-25 |title=Our work on building 5G-Advanced base stations will be a game changer: Debabrata Das, Director, IIIT Bangalore |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/technology/tech-news-technology/5g-advanced-base-stations-will-be-a-game-changer-debabrata-das-director-iiit-bangalore-9230265/ |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref>

=== Government ===
In 2021, the [[Ministry of Corporate Affairs]] introduced the first phase of MCA21 V3.0. It will allow for the electronic filing of documents under the [[corporate law]] and public access to corporate information. AI will be utilized by the platform to gather, organize, and classify stakeholder comments and inputs and produce analytical reports that will facilitate speedy policy choices.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2021-05-24 |title=Corporate Affairs Ministry launches first phase of MCA21 V3.0 portal |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/policy/corporate-affairs-ministry-launches-first-phase-of-mca21-v3-0-portal/articleshow/82910166.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-02-08 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref>

With assistance from [[Google]], the [[Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare]] and the [[Wadhwani Institute for Artificial Intelligence]] created Krishi 24/7, the first AI-powered automated agricultural news monitoring and analysis tool. Through better decision-making, Krishi 24/7 will support the identification of valuable news, provide timely notifications, and respond quickly to safeguard farmers' interests and advance sustainable agricultural growth. The application converts news articles into English after scanning them in several languages. It ensures that the ministry is informed in a timely manner about pertinent occurrences that are published online by extracting key information from news items, including the headline, crop name, event type, date, location, severity, summary, and source link. The [[National Centre for Disease Control|National Center for Disease Control]] has effectively implemented a comparable automated surveillance and analysis tool for disease outbreaks.<ref>{{Cite news |date=6 November 2023 |title=Krishi 24/7, the first-ever AI-powered solution for automated agricultural news monitoring and analysis |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1975109 |access-date=13 April 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]] |agency=Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India.}}</ref>

As part of the Safe City initiative, 1,000 AI cameras with [[Facial recognition system|facial recognition]] were placed at a cost of ₹96 [[crore]] in [[Lucknow]]'s commercial districts, colleges, hostels, large crossings, and public gathering spots. By integrating with the [[National Crime Records Bureau#National Automated Fingerprint Identification System|National Automated Fingerprint Identification System]], the cameras will detect suspicious movement of individuals by comparing their faces to a police database, notify control rooms of any criminal activities, and send out alerts against [[illegal dumping]]. For a more responsive and linked security network, AI will be included into [[Crisis hotline|crisis hotlines]] and [[Helpline|helplines]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-02-09 |title=In a 1st, 1K AI-enabled cameras to keep Lucknow safe and clean |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/lucknow/aienabled-cams-for-city-safety-and-cleanliness/articleshow/107542349.cms |access-date=2025-02-24 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

In collaboration with the [[Indian government]], IIIT-B created Datalake, a tool that analyzes government data on a range of projects to determine whether the objectives of the policy have been fulfilled and whether there is room for improvement. It can forecast how to modify the beneficiary structure to comply with the policy and benefit the citizens.<ref name=":4" />

The [[Government of Uttar Pradesh]] used [[Facial recognition system|facial recognition]] and AI-powered crowd density monitoring, RFID wristbands as part of the security setup for the [[2025 Prayag Maha Kumbh Mela]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=29 December 2024 |title=Maha Kumbh 2025: A Seamless and Spiritually Enriching Journey Awaits Devotees |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2088675 |access-date=24 February 2025 |work=Press Information Bureau |agency=Ministry of Culture, Government of India}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2024-12-30 |title=U.P. government to use AI-enabled cameras, RFID wristbands to track pilgrims at Mahakumbh |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/uttar-pradesh/up-government-to-use-ai-enabled-cameras-rfid-wristbands-to-track-pilgrims-at-mahakumbh/article69043950.ece |access-date=2025-02-24 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref> Plans to establish India's first AI lab aimed at strengthening cyber surveillance operations against [[deepfake]] threats and the country’s first tea auction driven by [[blockchain]] and AI, were announced by the [[Assam Government|Assam government]] in the state budget for 2025–2026.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kalita |first=Prabin |date=2025-03-10 |title=With Rs 2.6L-cr budget, Assam launches satellite plans, green & AI innovation |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/guwahati/with-rs-2-6l-cr-budget-assam-launches-satellite-plans-green-ai-innovation/articleshow/118856827.cms |access-date=2025-03-15 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> It will focus on real-time online threat detection, [[digital forensics]], and cybersecurity. The lab will track cyberthreats, and assess misleading media.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 March 2025 |title=Assam To Set Up India's First AI-Powered Anti-Deepfake & Cyber Surveillance Lab |url=https://www.guwahatiplus.com/assam/assam-to-set-up-indias-first-ai-powered-anti-deepfake-cyber-surveillance-lab |access-date=2025-03-15 |website=guwahatiplus.com |language=en}}</ref>

The AI Competency Framework was unveiled on 6 March 2025 by [[Ashwini Vaishnaw]], the [[Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology|Minister for Electronics and information Technology]], in recognition of the crucial role AI plays in governance. Its goal is to provide public sector professionals with the necessary skills for upskilling programs and AI competency mapping. This framework guarantees informed AI policy-making and implementation by conforming to international best practices. To improve government officials' iGOT Karmayogi platform learning experience, a tailored content suggestion system driven by AI was also unveiled.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":15" />  

=== Society ===
[[Wadhwani Institute for Artificial Intelligence|Wadhwani AI]], a $30 million nonprofit research institute, was established in 2018 by [[Romesh Wadhwani]] and [[Sunil Wadhwani]] with the goal of enhancing the lives of the world's poorest 2 billion people. [[New York University]], the [[University of Southern California]], [[Indian Institutes of Technology|India Institutes of Technology]], and [[University of Mumbai]] will collaborate with the institute. The objective is to have solutions that show how AI can help the [[underprivileged]], and then to build on those initial instances. Wadhwani AI will support universities from [[developing nations]] in expanding their AI capabilities.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cheney |first=Catherine |date=2018-02-21 |title=Indian billionaire brothers launch AI development research institute |url=https://www.devex.com/news/indian-billionaire-brothers-launch-ai-development-research-institute-92168 |access-date=2025-02-18 |website=Devex |language=en}}</ref> 

As part of [[Microsoft]]'s Global Skills for Social Impact charter, the ADVANTA(I)GE India program's first phase trained 2.4 million people in AI skills between 2024 and 2025; 74% of these persons came from [[Tier 2 cities in india|tier 2]] and [[Classification of Indian cities|tier 3]] cities, and 65% of them were women. Another 10 million people will be trained by 2030 as part of the second phase.<ref name=":16" /><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2024-02-07 |title=Microsoft to provide AI skilling opportunities to 2 million people in India by 2025 |url=https://news.microsoft.com/en-in/microsoft-to-provide-ai-skilling-opportunities-to-2-million-people-in-india-by-2025/ |access-date=2025-06-05 |website=Microsoft |language=en-IN}}</ref>

The [[Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology]] launched '''IndiaAI Application Development Initiative''' on 6 March 2025. The aim is to create, scale, and encourage the usage of AI to improve the socioeconomic landscape of the country. In order to solve issues in the fields of healthcare, agriculture, governance, [[Climate change in India|climate change]], [[Disaster management in India|disaster management]], and [[learning disabilities]], IndiaAI has initiated the '''IndiaAI''' '''Innovation Challenge'''. Enhancing access to public services, improving healthcare, increasing agricultural productivity, helping people with learning disabilities, and lessening the effects of climate change are the goals. With the goal of lowering entry barriers in the field of AI, the '''IndiaAI FutureSkills Initiative''' will expand the number of AI courses offered in undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral level. To deliver foundational level training, IndiaAI Data Labs are being set up in [[Tier 2 cities in india|tier 2]] and [[Classification of Indian cities|tier 3]] locations throughout the country. IndiaAI has created the two courses for the positions of Data Curator and Data Annotator, with an emphasis on industries like manufacturing, healthcare, education, and agriculture. These will be taught in IndiaAI Data Labs located throughout 28 centers of the [[National Institute of Electronics & Information Technology]], and [[Industrial training institute|industrial training institutes]].<ref name=":14" /><ref>{{Cite news |date=19 March 2025 |title=Government of India Expands AI-Driven Skilling |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2113095 |access-date=4 June 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]] |agency=Ministry of Electronics & IT, Government of India.}}</ref>

An MoU was signed on 5 June 2025, between [[OpenAI]] and the IndiaAI Mission to establish OpenAI Academy, which would provide AI education training materials in Hindi, English, and four regional languages for students, developers, educators, civil servants, nonprofit leaders, and small business owners.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Sadashiv |first=Sakshi |date=5 June 2025 |title=OpenAI signs MoU with IndiaAI Mission to launch OpenAI Academy in India |url=https://www.livemint.com/technology/tech-news/openai-signs-mou-with-indiaai-mission-to-launch-openai-academy-in-india-11749131568891.html |access-date=12 June 2025 |work=livemint.com}}</ref> It will integrate with IndiaAI FutureSkills Initiative and iGOT Karmayogi platform. One million teachers will receive training on how to use GenAI in the classroom. Additionally, 50 startups or fellows recognized by the IndiaAI Mission will get API credits from OpenAI worth up to $100,000.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Choudhary |first=Govind |date=2025-06-05 |title=OpenAI launches first global education platform in India in partnership with IndiaAI Mission |url=https://www.livemint.com/technology/tech-news/openai-launches-first-global-education-platform-in-india-in-partnership-with-indiaai-mission-11749131822971.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250607083416/https://www.livemint.com/technology/tech-news/openai-launches-first-global-education-platform-in-india-in-partnership-with-indiaai-mission-11749131822971.html |archive-date=2025-06-07 |access-date=2025-06-12 |work=livemint.com |language=en}}</ref> OpenAI has extended its '''AI for Impact Accelerator program''' by giving 11 [[NGOs]] a total of $150,000 in technical funding to develop AI solutions for underserved industries like healthcare, education, and agriculture.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Roy |first=Supriya |date=2025-06-03 |title=OpenAI Academy expands to India, commits $150,000 to nonprofits |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/openai-academy-expands-to-india-commits-150000-to-nonprofits/articleshow/121602608.cms |access-date=2025-06-12 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

=== Finance and insurance ===
In India's [[BFSI|banking, financial services and insurance]] (BFSI) industries, AI is already in use as of 2024 and the use of AI by BFSI companies is growing.<ref name=":13">{{Cite web |date=6 November 2024 |title=AI, GenAI, and blockchain: How technology is transforming BFSI sector |url=https://www.business-standard.com/technology/tech-news/ai-genai-and-blockchain-how-technology-is-transforming-bfsi-sector-124110501372_1.html |access-date=20 May 2025 |website=Business Standard}}</ref> Banks in India are using it for [[predictive analytics]], fraud detection, and personalisation services.<ref name=":13" /> In capital markets, AI is being used for [[high-frequency trading]] and [[Quantitative analysis (finance)|quantitative analysis]].<ref name=":13" /> AI is being used by insurance companies for underwriting, fraud detection and damage assessment.<ref name=":13" /> However, with the growth of AI usage in the BFSI sector, the Indian government has also stated that AI, including deepfakes and prompt hacking of large language models, is being used for cyberattacks on BFSI companies.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Doval |first=Pankaj |date=7 April 2025 |title=Govt-backed report warns of threats to BFSI from deep fakes and AI-generated content |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/govt-backed-report-warns-of-threats-to-bfsi-from-deep-fakes-and-ai-generated-content/articleshow/120071326.cms |access-date=20 May 2025 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

== Safety and regulation ==
In order to determine whether to create an [[AI Safety Institute]] (AISI) that can establish standards, frameworks, and guidelines for AI development without serving as a regulatory body or stifling innovation, [[MeitY]] conducted consultation process with [[Meta Platforms]], [[Google]], [[Microsoft]], [[IBM]], [[OpenAI]], [[NASSCOM]], Broadband India Forum, [[Software Alliance]], [[Indian Institutes of Technology]], The Quantum Hub, Digital Empowerment Foundation, and [[Access Now]] on 7 October 2024. It was decided that instead of focusing on regulation, the AISI would focus on damage detection, risk identification, and standards setting for which interoperable systems are necessary to prevent the development of silos which may eventually influence future policies. The Safe and Trusted Pillar of the IndiaAI Mission has been allocated [[₹]]20 [[crore]], which the AISI may use for the inaugural budget. More money from the IndiaAI Mission's other verticals may be used in the future.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-10-13 |title=Govt mulls setting up Artificial Intelligence Safety Institute |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/govt-mulls-setting-up-artificial-intelligence-safety-institute-101728833433153.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241120105636/https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/govt-mulls-setting-up-artificial-intelligence-safety-institute-101728833433153.html |archive-date=2024-11-20 |access-date=2025-02-17 |work=Hindustan Times |language=en-us}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jeevanandam |first=Nivash |date=15 October 2024 |title=MeitY Hosts Consultation for Establishing India AI Safety Institute under IndiaAI Mission's Safe and Trusted Pillar |url=https://indiaai.gov.in/news/meity-hosts-consultation-for-establishing-india-ai-safety-institute-under-indiaai-mission-s-safe-and-trusted-pillar |access-date=2025-02-17 |website=IndiaAI |language=en}}</ref>

In order to develop an AI policy report tailored to India and assess the country's AI ecosystem's strengths and future prospects, [[UNESCO]] and MeitY began consulting on AI Readiness Assessment Methodology under Safety and Ethics in Artificial Intelligence from 2024. It is to encourage the ethical and responsible use of AI in industries. The study will help find areas where government can become involved, especially in attempts to strengthen institutional and regulatory capabilities.<ref>{{Cite news |date=16 November 2024 |title=UNESCO and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Host Multi-Stakeholder Consultation on Safety and Ethics in Artificial Intelligence |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2073920 |access-date=19 February 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]] |agency=Ministry of Electronics & IT, Government of India}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=21 January 2025 |title=UNESCO and Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) host stakeholder consultation on AI Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM) in India |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2094899 |access-date=19 February 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]] |agency=Ministry of Electronics & IT, Government of India}}</ref>

[[Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology|Minister for Electronics & Information Technology]] [[Ashwini Vaishnaw]] announced the creation of an [[IndiaAI Safety Institute]] on 30 January 2025, to ensure the ethical and safe application of AI models. The institute will promote domestic [[research and development]] that is grounded in India's social, economic, cultural, and linguistic diversity and is based on Indian datasets. With the help of academic and research institutions, as well as private sector partners, the institute will follow the [[hub-and-spoke]] approach to carry out projects within Safe and Trusted Pillar of the IndiaAI Mission. Among the major safety-related initiatives are eight ongoing projects to implement a techno-legal strategy to protect data privacy while conducting an ethical audit of algorithmic effectiveness.<ref name=":5" />

First round of projects are as follows:<ref>{{Cite web |title=Annexure 3 |url=https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/jan/doc2025130492201.pdf |access-date=25 February 2025 |website=Press Information Bureau}}</ref>

[[Infosys]] released an open-source "Responsible AI" toolbox on 26 February 2025. The program, is a component of the Infosys Topaz Responsible AI Suite. It assists in identifying and stopping security risks, privacy violations, biased outputs, damaging content, copyright infringement, false information, deepfakes, and the use of malevolent AI. The toolkit can improve the transparency of outcomes produced by AI. It works with both on-premises and cloud systems.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 February 2025 |title=Infosys Unveils Open Source 'Responsible AI' Toolkit To Promote Ethical Use |url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/infosys-unveils-open-source-responsible-ai-toolkit-to-promote-ethical-use-7799415 |access-date=2025-02-27 |website=ndtv.com |language=en}}</ref> Citing concerns about the confidentiality of government data and documents, the [[Ministry of Finance (India)|Ministry of Finance]] issued an internal department caution advising staff not to use AI tools like [[ChatGPT]] and [[DeepSeek (chatbot)|DeepSeek]] for work-related purposes.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Singh |first1=Sarita |last2=Ohri |first2=Nikunj |date=5 February 2025 |title=India's finance ministry asks employees to avoid AI tools like ChatGPT, DeepSeek |url=https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/indias-finance-ministry-asks-employees-avoid-ai-tools-like-chatgpt-deepseek-2025-02-05/ |access-date=3 March 2025 |work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> 

In order to comply with the [[Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023]] and other sovereignty requirements, [[OpenAI]] allowed the local storage of data for ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Edu, and OpenAI [[API]] platform customers from 8 May 2025.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Aryan |first=Aashish |date=8 May 2025 |title=OpenAI to store ChatGPT Enterprise and API user data locally in India |url=https://www.business-standard.com/technology/tech-news/openai-chatgpt-india-data-residency-enterprise-edu-api-launch-125050800140_1.html |access-date=12 June 2025 |work=[[Business Standard]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Lohchab |first=Himanshi |date=2025-05-20 |title=ET Explainer: What OpenAI's local data residency means for India |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/artificial-intelligence/et-explainer-what-openais-local-data-residency-means-for-india/articleshow/121275267.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-06-12 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref> Talks to establish data center operations in India have already been started by OpenAI.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Aryan |first=Aashish |date=13 February 2025 |title=ChatGPT maker OpenAI's plan to set up India data centre in the works |url=https://www.business-standard.com/technology/tech-news/chatgpt-maker-openai-s-plan-to-set-up-india-data-centre-in-the-works-125021301533_1.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250220163942/https://www.business-standard.com/technology/tech-news/chatgpt-maker-openai-s-plan-to-set-up-india-data-centre-in-the-works-125021301533_1.html |archive-date=2025-02-20 |access-date=2025-06-12 |website=Business Standard |language=en-US}}</ref> 

[[Google]] launched its Safety Charter for India's AI-led transformation on 18 June 2025. Keeping end users safe, cybersecurity for government and enterprise infrastructure, and responsibly developing AI are the three core pillars that it outlines for addressing the difficulties of the online world in partnership with the larger ecosystem.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mishra |first=Urvashi |date=2025-06-18 |title=Google unveils Safety Charter to secure India's AI-powered digital future |url=https://www.fortuneindia.com/technology/google-unveils-safety-charter-to-secure-indias-ai-powered-digital-future/124147 |access-date=2025-06-20 |website=Fortune India |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jain |first=Ayushi |date=2025-06-17 |title=As AI grows, Google introduces Safety Charter in India to fight scams and boost cybersecurity |url=https://www.digit.in/news/general/as-ai-grows-google-rolls-out-safety-charter-in-india-to-fight-scams-and-boost-cybersecurity.html |access-date=2025-06-20 |website=Digit |language=en}}</ref> In order to operationalize Google's Safety Charter, Google Safety Engineering Center in [[Hyderabad]] was established.<ref>{{Cite web |last=John |first=Merin Susan |date=2025-06-19 |title=Google Opens Cybersecurity Hub in Hyderabad to Strengthen India's Digital Safety Infra |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/google-opens-cybersecurity-hub-in-hyderabad-to-strengthen-indias-digital-safety-infra/ |access-date=2025-06-20 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

The '''BlackBerry Priv''' is a [[Slider (mobile phones)|slider]] [[smartphone]] developed by [[BlackBerry Limited]]. Following a series of leaks, it was officially announced by BlackBerry CEO [[John S. Chen|John Chen]] on September 25, 2015, and released on November 6, 2015.<ref name=techcrunch-privpreorder>{{cite web|title=Priv, The Android Phone With A Physical Keyboard, Goes Up For Pre-Order|url=https://techcrunch.com/2015/10/23/priv-pre-orders/|website=TechCrunch|date=23 October 2015 |publisher=AOL|access-date=3 November 2015}}</ref> The Priv was the first [[BlackBerry]] smartphone that does not run the company's in-house [[BlackBerry OS]] or [[BlackBerry 10]] (BB10) platforms, instead running [[Android (operating system)|Android]], customized with features inspired by those on BlackBerry phones, and security enhancements. 

With its use of Android—one of two smartphone platforms that significantly impacted BlackBerry's early dominance in the smartphone industry—the company sought to leverage access to the larger ecosystem of software available through the [[Google Play Store]] (as opposed to BlackBerry 10 devices, which were limited to native BB10 apps from [[BlackBerry World]] and Android apps from the third-party [[Amazon Appstore]] running in a compatibility subsystem), in combination with a slide-out physical keyboard and privacy-focused features.<ref name=gandm-bbpriv/>

The BlackBerry Priv received mixed reviews. Critics praised the Priv's user experience for incorporating BlackBerry's traditional, productivity-oriented features on top of the standard Android experience, including a notifications feed and custom e-mail client. Some critics felt that the device's physical keyboard did not perform as well as those on previous BlackBerry devices, and that the Priv's performance was not up to par with other devices using the same system-on-chip. The Priv was also criticized for being more expensive than similarly equipped devices in its class.<ref name="verge-review"/><ref name="wsj-review"/><ref name="ars-review"/> It was the final BlackBerry device internally designed by BlackBerry Limited; subsequent Android-based BlackBerry products would be branded under [[BlackBerry Mobile]] and designed by [[TCL Corporation]] for the global market, and select third-party [[Original equipment manufacturer|OEMs]] for certain emerging markets.

== Development ==
While BlackBerry was dominant in the early smartphone market, partially due to a large market share within the enterprise and governmental markets, the company had struggled in recent years due to the worldwide statistical dominance of the plethora of [[Android (operating system)|Android]] smartphones, and [[Apple Inc.]] and its [[iPhone]] line, the biggest maker of [[Android (operating system)|Android]] devices being [[Samsung Electronics]].<ref name=wsj-pinshopes>{{cite news|title=BlackBerry Pins Hopes for First Android Device Priv on Security Cachet|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/blackberry-pins-hopes-for-first-android-device-priv-on-security-cachet-1446480000|access-date=3 November 2015|work=The Wall Street Journal|date=November 2, 2015}}</ref> By June 2015, the company's market share in the U.S. consumer market had fallen to 1.2%.<ref name="jun2015">{{cite web|title=comScore Reports June 2015 U.S. Smartphone Subscriber Market Share|url=http://www.comscore.com/Insights/Market-Rankings/comScore-Reports-June-2015-US-Smartphone-Subscriber-Market-Share|access-date=13 August 2015|publisher=[[comScore]]|date=7 August 2015}}</ref> Facing a struggling ecosystem for native, third-party software on [[BlackBerry 10]], BlackBerry added a compatibility layer for Android software to the OS, and allowed developers to repackage their Android apps for distribution on [[BlackBerry World]]. Later versions added the ability for users to manually install Android [[APK file|app packages]]. Beginning with the [[BlackBerry Passport]], [[Amazon Appstore]] was bundled with BlackBerry 10 to provide an additional source of third-party Android software.<ref name=pcmag-28kandroid>{{cite web|title=How BlackBerry 10 Runs 28,000 Android Apps Without a Back Button|url=https://www.pcmag.com/article2/0,2817,2414928,00.asp|website=PC Magazine|access-date=18 June 2014}}</ref><ref name=pcmag-runhere>{{cite web|title=BlackBerry: Run Your Android Apps Here!|url=https://www.pcmag.com/article2/0,2817,2454097,00.asp|website=PC Magazine|access-date=18 June 2014}}</ref><ref name=verge-amazonapp>{{cite web|title=BlackBerry will bring thousands of apps from Amazon's store to its phones|url=https://www.theverge.com/2014/6/18/5820472/blackberry-phones-getting-amazon-appstore-apps-in-bb10-3|website=The Verge|date=18 June 2014 |access-date=18 June 2014}}</ref> BlackBerry CEO [[John S. Chen]] hoped that Amazon's own smartphone, the [[Fire Phone]], would bolster the adoption of the Amazon store and attract more major developers to it, and in turn, BlackBerry's ecosystem. However, the Fire Phone was a commercial failure, which led to BlackBerry's decision to develop an Android phone of its own.<ref name=gandm-bbpriv>{{cite news|title=BlackBerry bets on Android's apps to buoy new Priv|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/technology/tech-news/blackberry-revenue-falls-short-adjusted-loss-more-than-expected/article26539263/|access-date=26 September 2015|work=The Globe & Mail}}</ref>

In early 2014, BlackBerry's device head Ron Louks proposed that the company construct an Android device. Company officials, including Chen, showed concerns over the project, as they believed the platform was not secure enough. However, Louks gained support for the project after outlining plans for hardware-based security.<ref name=cnet-winyouover/> At [[Mobile World Congress]] 2015, BlackBerry's device head Ron Louks briefly presented a non-functioning prototype of a new, BlackBerry 10 phone that featured a sliding keyboard and a screen curved across both sides, similar to the [[Samsung Galaxy S6 Edge]] that was unveiled during the same convention.<ref name=cnet-winyouover>{{cite web|title=Inside BlackBerry's last-ditch plan to win you back with Android|url=http://www.cnet.com/news/inside-blackberrys-last-ditch-plan-to-win-you-back-with-android/|website=CNET|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=3 November 2015}}</ref><ref name=bbcnews-s6unveil>{{cite news|title=Samsung S6 Edge with curved screen unveiled at MWC|work=BBC News |date=March 2015 |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-31645426|access-date=1 March 2015}}</ref><ref name=phonearena-teased>{{cite web|title=BlackBerry teased a curved screen slider at MWC 2015|url=http://www.gsmarena.com/blackberry_teased_a_curved_screen_slider_at_mwc_2015-news-11404.php|website=PhoneArena|access-date=26 September 2015}}</ref> In July 2015, new images of the curved device leaked under the codename "Venice"; unlike the version presented at MWC, it was now shown to be running [[Android (operating system)|Android]] [[Android Lollipop|5.0 "Lollipop"]] rather than BlackBerry 10.<ref name=zdnet-veniceleak>{{cite web|title=BlackBerry Venice may be the company's first Android slider|url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/blackberry-venice-may-be-the-companys-first-android-slider/|website=ZDNet|access-date=26 September 2015}}</ref> Information about the device's software leaked in August 2015, showing a "stock" Android experience augmented with ports of features and apps from BB10, such as BlackBerry Hub.<ref name=engadget-venicesoftware>{{cite web|title=BlackBerry's Android phone should include a ton of BB10 features|url=https://www.engadget.com/2015/08/23/blackberry-venice-software-leak/|website=Engadget|date=23 August 2015 |access-date=26 September 2015}}</ref>

In response to the leaks, Chen officially confirmed during a September 2015 earnings call that BlackBerry would release a high-end Android-based device, now known as the Priv (standing for both "privilege" and "privacy"), in late 2015.<ref>{{cite news|title=BlackBerry to Launch Android Smartphone|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/blackberry-to-launch-android-smartphone-1443181465|website=Wall Street Journal|date=25 September 2015 |publisher=Dow Jones & Company|access-date=25 September 2015|last1=Dummett |first1=Ben }}</ref>  Chen felt that the decision to produce an Android phone was to help BlackBerry's device business sustain itself, saying that "we have some really committed diehards. I respect that there's a lot of heritage here, a lot of pride. If the math doesn't add up, the math doesn't add up. We could keep the pride and die hungry or we can eat well and not so proud, maybe. So I chose to eat well. It's good for the company to continue to have a shot at building handsets."<ref name=gandm-bbpriv/> He also argued that the decision was meant to "[take] advantage of what the industry can offer", whilst continuing to leverage BlackBerry's "core strength".<ref name=recode-mayquit/>

BlackBerry promoted certain security enhancements made to the build of Android bundled with the Priv, which include utilizing features of its [[System on a chip|SoC]] to embed unchangeable cryptographic keys in the device hardware which are used to validate critical boot components, thus establishing a "root of trust" designed to foil attempts to tamper with the OS.<ref name=qualcomm-snapdragon-security>{{cite web|title=Snapdragon Mobile Security for Embedded Devices, Biometric Authentication and SafeSwitch Technology|url=https://www.qualcomm.com/products/snapdragon/security|website=Qualcomm|access-date=22 November 2015}}</ref><ref name=ARM-security-TrustZone>{{cite web|title=ARM Security Technology Building a Secure System using TrustZone Technology: 5.2.2. Secure boot|url=http://infocenter.arm.com/help/topic/com.arm.doc.prd29-genc-009492c/CACGCHFE.html|website=ARM|access-date=22 November 2015}}</ref> Additionally, kernel security enhancements are mentioned. (Provided by grsecurity)<ref name=androidauthority-priv-leak-photos>{{cite web|title=Blackberry Venice rumors: release date, price, specs, features|url=http://www.androidauthority.com/blackberry-venice-rumors-release-date-price-specs-features-638396/|website=Android Authority|date=20 September 2015 |access-date=22 November 2015}}</ref> BlackBerry also promoted that storage encryption would be enabled by default on the Priv, as well as a general company commitment to timely patch releases for known Android security vulnerabilities, subject to carrier approval.<ref name=BlackBerry-Priv-security-features>{{cite web|title=Security features for PRIV by BlackBerry - BES12 - 12.3|url=https://help.blackberry.com/en/bes12/12.3/security/kja1444235374663.html|website=BlackBerry|access-date=22 November 2015|archive-date=23 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151123145827/https://help.blackberry.com/en/bes12/12.3/security/kja1444235374663.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=BlackBerry-Managing-Priv-Patching>{{cite web|title=Managing Android Security Patching for PRIV - Inside BlackBerry|url=http://blogs.blackberry.com/2015/11/managing-android-security-patching-for-priv/|website=BlackBerry|access-date=22 November 2015|archive-date=23 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151123141643/http://blogs.blackberry.com/2015/11/managing-android-security-patching-for-priv/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The company stated that BlackBerry 10 devices would continue to co-exist alongside Android-based devices; BlackBerry COO Marty Beard explained that BlackBerry 10 is able to meet "very high-end security needs" that cannot currently be met by Android, while Chen reported that the platform has seen adoption in enterprise and governmental markets. Chen stated that he would consider dropping BlackBerry 10 if his company were able to port all of its security features to Android.<ref name=recode-mayquit>{{cite web|title=BlackBerry May Quit Handsets if It Can't Make Money by Next Year, Says CEO John Chen|url=http://recode.net/2015/10/08/blackberry-may-quit-handsets-if-it-cant-make-money-by-next-year-says-ceo-john-chen/|website=Re/code|date=8 October 2015|publisher=Vox Media|access-date=3 November 2015|archive-date=8 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151108011424/http://recode.net/2015/10/08/blackberry-may-quit-handsets-if-it-cant-make-money-by-next-year-says-ceo-john-chen/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=nyt-priv>{{cite news|title=BlackBerry Unveils an Android-Powered Phone With Security Features|url=http://bits.blogs.nytimes.com/2015/11/02/blackberry-unveils-an-android-powered-phone-with-security-features/?_r=0|access-date=3 November 2015|work=The New York Times| date=2 November 2015 }}</ref> However, BlackBerry has not released any new BlackBerry 10-powered devices since, and discontinued its [[BlackBerry Classic]] in July 2016.<ref name="gandm-classicdisc">{{cite web|title=BlackBerry to stop making Classic smartphone|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/report-on-business/blackberry-to-stop-making-blackberry-classic-smartphone/article30754260/|website=The Globe and Mail|access-date=27 July 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theverge.com/2016/2/27/11127508/whatsapp-blackberry-nokia-discontinued |title=WhatsApp will be discontinued on BlackBerry and Nokia operating systems by 2017 |last=D'Orazio |first=Dante |date=February 27, 2016 |website=The Verge |publisher=Vox media |access-date=July 27, 2016}}</ref>

== Specifications ==

=== Hardware ===
The Priv features a {{convert|5.43|in|mm|abbr=on}}, [[1440p]] [[AMOLED]] display, which is slightly curved around the horizontal sides of the device. The rear of the device is coated in a "glass weave" material.<ref name=verge-review/> The screen can be slid up to reveal a hardware keyboard; similar to the [[BlackBerry Passport]], the keyboard is touch-sensitive and can register sliding gestures across its keys for scrolling, text selection, and autocomplete suggestions.<ref name=ars-firstreview>{{cite web|title=Blackberry Priv early impressions: This is (currently) not a very good phone|url=https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2015/11/two-days-with-the-blackberry-priv-it-needs-to-be-better/|website=Ars Technica|date=6 November 2015 |access-date=6 November 2015}}</ref> a bezel on the left acts as a power button whilst two bezels on the right act as volume up/down buttons separately. Unlike the Passport, the shorter, shallower key can only be used as a mute button (on the passport this key called up the assistant). The Priv utilizes a hexa-core [[Snapdragon (system on chip)#Snapdragon 808|Snapdragon 808]] system-on-chip with 3&nbsp;GB of RAM, consisting of four low-power [[Cortex-A53]] cores and two [[Cortex-A57]] cores, and includes a non-removable 3420&nbsp;mAh battery which BlackBerry claims can last for 22-and-a-half hours of "mixed use".<ref name=verge-review/> The Priv includes 32&nbsp;GB of internal storage, with the option to expand the amount of available storage using a microSD card up to 2&nbsp;TB in size. The device features an 18-megapixel rear-facing camera with [[phase detection autofocus]] and [[optical image stabilization]], and a 2-megapixel front camera.<ref name=ars-privunveil>{{cite web|title=BlackBerry's first Android phone ships November 6th for $699|url=https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2015/10/blackberrys-first-android-phone-ships-november-6th-for-699/|website=Ars Technica|date=23 October 2015 |access-date=3 November 2015}}</ref>

=== Software ===
The Priv shipped with [[Android Lollipop|Android 5.1.1 "Lollipop"]] a month after [[Android Marshmallow|Android 6.0 Marshmallow]] was launched, using a "stock" user experience customized with additional features and BlackBerry-developed apps. BlackBerry Hub (which originates from BlackBerry 10)<ref name=engadget-venicesoftware /> aggregates notifications and content from multiple sources and allows for granular management of messages and "snoozing" based on time, location or network availability. Hub can also be accessed alongside BlackBerry Search and [[Google Search]] options when swiping from the bottom of the screen.<ref name=ars-firstreview/> The "Productivity Edge" feature allows a tab to be shown on either the left or right curve of the display, which can be dragged out to display an agenda screen. A progress bar can also be displayed on an edge when the device is charging.<ref name=pa-edge>{{cite web|title=The BlackBerry Priv features a Productivity Edge (thanks to its curved display)|url=http://www.phonearena.com/news/The-BlackBerry-Priv-features-a-Productivity-Edge-thanks-to-its-curved-display_id75105|website=PhoneArena|date=26 October 2015 }}</ref> An application's home screen widget can be made available from its respective shortcut icon by swiping, which displays the widget as a pop-up window.<ref name=cnet-bbads/> The DTEK app allows users to view an overview of the security and privacy status of the device based on best practices, and provide notifications when apps attempt to access sensitive information or permissions.<ref name=verge-review/> The Priv also integrates with the pre-existing [[Android for Work]] suite, which allows personal and work-oriented data on a device to be segregated (similarly to the BlackBerry Balance features on BB10).<ref name=cnet-bbads>{{cite web|title=BlackBerry touts its Android Priv phone in new video spots|url=http://www.cnet.com/news/blackberry-touts-its-android-priv-phone-in-new-video-spots/|website=CNET|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=3 November 2015}}</ref><ref name=zdnet-privsecurity>{{cite web|title=The many ways BlackBerry beefs up Android security on the Priv|url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/the-many-ways-blackberry-beefs-up-android-security-on-the-priv/|website=ZDNet|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=3 November 2015}}</ref><ref name=zdnet-privstandout>{{cite web|title=BlackBerry Priv standout features: Hub, pop-up widgets and security app|url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/blackberry-priv-standout-features-hub-pop-up-widgets-and-security-app/|website=ZDNet|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=3 November 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=BlackBerry Promises Robust Security on Android-Based Priv|url=https://www.pcmag.com/article2/0,2817,2493584,00.asp|website=PC Magazine|access-date=26 October 2015}}</ref>

In late-April 2016, BlackBerry began to release an upgrade to [[Android Marshmallow|Android 6.0 "Marshmallow"]];<ref name="gsmarena-marsh"/> along with features added to the core Android platform (which includes a new permissions system, and systems to reduce background activity when the device is not being physically handled to conserve battery power),<ref name=android-doze>{{cite news|title=Optimizing for Doze and App Standby|url=http://developer.android.com/training/monitoring-device-state/doze-standby.html#whitelisting-cases|access-date=17 November 2015|work=Android developers portal}}</ref> it adds [[S/MIME]], [[Slack (software)|Slack]], [[Skype]], and [[Pinterest]] support to BlackBerry Hub, slide input on the physical keyboard, faster autofocus, and 24&nbsp;fps and 120&nbsp;fps video recording modes.<ref name="gsmarena-marsh">{{cite web|title=BlackBerry Priv gets Android 6.0 Marshmallow|url=http://www.gsmarena.com/blackberry_priv_gets_android_60_marshmallow-news-17962.php|website=GSMArena|access-date=27 July 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theverge.com/2016/4/26/11511210/blackberry-priv-android-marshmallow |title=The Blackberry Priv is getting Marshmallow and a sweet swipe keyboard |last=Carman |first=Ashley |date=April 26, 2016 |website=The Verge |publisher=Vox Media |access-date=July 27, 2016}}</ref>

The Priv was not updated to [[Android Nougat|Android 7.0 "Nougat"]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gsmarena.com/no_nougat_update_for_priv_blackberry_confirms-news-27190.php|title=No Nougat update for Priv, BlackBerry confirms|website=GSMArena.com|language=en-US|access-date=2019-02-10}}</ref> Regular security updates ended in December 2017, although out-of-band updates would still be released in case of critical vulnerabilities.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://crackberry.com/blackberry-priv-will-no-longer-receive-monthly-updates-going-forward|title=BlackBerry Priv will no longer receive monthly security updates going forward|date=2017-12-14|website=CrackBerry.com|language=en|access-date=2019-02-10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.phonearena.com/news/BlackBerry-Priv-receives-unexpected-update_id103821|title=BlackBerry Priv receives unexpected update|last=Friedman|first=Alan|website=Phone Arena|date=5 April 2018 |language=en-US|access-date=2019-02-10}}</ref>

Similarly to the Passport, there is unofficial development work being done to port [[android 11]] to the Blackberry Priv.<ref>{{Cite web |last=guizmox44 |date=2024-09-30 |title=Lineage OS 18.1 - Priv and Passport |url=https://www.reddit.com/r/blackberry/comments/1ft4q4e/lineage_os_181_priv_and_passport/?rdt=52930 |access-date=2024-10-17 |website=r/blackberry}}</ref> The work is based on LineageOS 18.1 and is still a work in progress. Along with the Passport, the development work has taken place in Discord.

== Reception ==
The Priv received mixed reviews. ''[[The Verge]]'' felt that the Priv's design was "quite good", noting that the thinness of the device's two halves averted it from feeling "top-heavy" when its keyboard was in use.<ref name="verge-review"/> ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' described the frame and curved screen as being "a pleasure to hold and look at."<ref name="wsj-review"/> ''[[Ars Technica]]'' was critical of the device's overall build quality, with its back cover described as feeling "spongy" its sliding mechanism described as being "scratchy" and "friction-filled", while its curved screen was considered a "rather useless gimmick" that was inappropriate for the device's target market.<ref name="ars-review"/> ''Ars Technica'' also panned the hardware mute button for being "counterintuitive", as it does not mute the device unless it is already playing audio, otherwise triggering the system volume controls.<ref name="ars-review"/> The hardware keyboard received mixed reviews. ''The Wall Street Journal'' described the keyboard as being the "smartphone equivalent of a Colonial [[butter churn]]", noting that, although it was faster to type on in comparison to virtual keyboards, the [[BlackBerry Classic]] had a larger and wider keyboard.<ref name="wsj-review"/> ''Ars Technica'' felt it was "unpleasant" to use due to its size, flat keys and how it interacts with the OS.<ref name="ars-review"/> ''[[PC Magazine]]'' described its display as being "beautiful",<ref name=pcmag-privreview/> while ''Ars Technica'' felt that it had "grainy" color reproduction.<ref name="ars-review"/>

In regards to performance, ''PC Magazine'' described the Priv as having "(benchmarked) like (an [[LG G4]]) that's been throttled down after some gaming", noting that its [[AnTuTu]] scores were lower than those of the [[Nexus 6P]] and [[Samsung Galaxy S6]]. It also noted that while it wasn't "technically" unresponsive, "there are some complex animations and missed touch or typing inputs that might make you feel like it is".<ref name=pcmag-privreview>{{cite web|title=BlackBerry Priv (Unlocked)|url=https://www.pcmag.com/article2/0,2817,2494378,00.asp|website=PC Magazine|access-date=26 November 2015}}</ref> ''The Wall Street Journal'' felt that the Priv felt "inexcusably slow" at times, reporting instances of slow or unresponsive apps.<ref name="wsj-review"/> The battery life was praised, with ''The Wall Street Journal'' remarking that it "outran" the [[Nexus 5X]], 6P and [[iPhone 6S]],<ref name="wsj-review"/> while ''PC Magazine'' credited its aggressive suppression of background activity as improving its standby battery life, stating that it survived a weekend of use with 25% capacity still remaining.<ref name=pcmag-privreview/> In contrast, ''The Verge'' and ''Ars Technica'' claimed they were unable to reach the device's advertised battery life.<ref name="verge-review"/> ''PC Magazine'' praised the Priv's call quality, noting that it had a clear microphone and "delivers very loud maximum speakerphone and earpiece volume with zero distortion or wobble."<ref name=pcmag-privreview/> The Priv's rear-facing camera was criticized for having autofocus issues and for producing washed-out images with poor contrast and low-light performance.<ref name="ars-review"/><ref name=pcmag-privreview/>

''[[Ars Technica]]'' approved of the phone's software for staying close to Android's default user experience while providing optional enhancements, but noted that it did not ship with the latest version of Android. BlackBerry Hub was also praised by ''The Verge'' allowing users to "filter all of [their notifications] in a million different ways to get super productive views of what you need to get done really quickly", but criticized for not supporting all services and for not allowing users to archive messages from [[Gmail]] within the interface. ''PC Magazine'' noted that some of the features BlackBerry added to Android could be accomplished with widgets on other devices.<ref name=pcmag-privreview/> ''The Wall Street Journal'' felt that most of the enhancements to the OS were useful and the email interface was "[trumping] all others when it comes to formatting options", although it was slower than the Gmail app. The focus on user privacy was described as "not running very deep"; although the DTEK app and its privacy suggestions were well received, it was noted that most of the improvements to privacy and security were not exclusive to the Priv and that the hardened kernel, while making the phone more secure in theory, had not been externally [[Information technology security audit|audited]].<ref name="wsj-review"/> ''PC Magazine'' similarly questioned the security features, noting that [[Android Marshmallow|Android "Marshmallow"]] allows app permissions to be revoked individually (a function not implemented by DTEK) and supports device encryption, and that using Google services requires users to agree to data collection by the company to begin with.<ref name=pcmag-privreview/>

The Priv was also criticized for its high price in comparison to other recent "flagship" phones with better specifications.<ref name="verge-review"/><ref name="wsj-review"/><ref name="ars-review"/> In conclusion, while commending BlackBerry for being in "way better shape with the Priv than it was with any of its BB10 devices", the Priv was ultimately described by ''Ars Technica'' as being "passable" and recommended the Nexus 6P as a cheaper alternative.<ref name="ars-review">{{Cite web|title = BlackBerry Priv review: Android fixes the OS, but the hardware can't compete|url = http://arstechnica.co.uk/gadgets/2015/11/blackberry-priv-review-android-fixes-the-os-but-the-hardware-cant-compete/|website = [[Ars Technica]]|access-date = November 12, 2015|date = November 12, 2015|last = Amadeo|first = Ron}}</ref> ''The Wall Street Journal'' felt that the Priv was "a really good phone for people who want a [hardware] keyboard and a more secure Android experience", but that it "isn't going to put BlackBerry back on top again".<ref name="wsj-review">{{Cite news|title = BlackBerry Priv Review: BlackBerry May Win You Back With Android|url = https://www.wsj.com/articles/blackberry-priv-review-blackberry-may-win-you-back-with-android-1446786132|newspaper = The Wall Street Journal|access-date = November 18, 2015|first = Joanna|last = Stern|date = November 6, 2015}}</ref> ''The Verge'' felt that the Priv was a "remarkable" debut for Android on BlackBerry hardware, albeit marred by its performance issues.<ref name="verge-review">{{cite web|title=BlackBerry Priv review|url=https://www.theverge.com/2015/11/9/9694374/blackberry-priv-review-android-phone|website=The Verge|date=9 November 2015 |access-date=11 November 2015}}</ref>

=== Sales ===
BlackBerry did not provide specific sales numbers for the Priv, only stating in April 2016 that it had sold a total of 650,000 devices during the fiscal quarter ending February 29, 2016, and that these numbers were down from its original projection of 800,000. An unnamed AT&T executive stated to ''CNET'' that a large number of customers were returning the device, and that the company believed BlackBerry had priced the Priv too high.<ref name="cnet-worse">{{cite web|title=BlackBerry Priv is faring worse than expected|url=https://www.cnet.com/news/blackberry-priv-may-have-done-worse-than-we-thought/|website=CNET|access-date=2 October 2016}}</ref>

======================================================================
WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: Computer security
======================================================================

{{Short description|Protection of computer systems from information disclosure, theft or damage}}
{{Use American English|date=August 2024}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=February 2021}}
{{Computer hacking}}
{{OS}}

'''Computer security''' (also '''cybersecurity''', '''digital security''', or '''information technology''' ('''IT''') '''security''') is a subdiscipline within the field of [[information security]]. It focuses on protecting [[computer software]], [[system]]s, and [[computer network|networks]] from [[Threat (security)|threats]] that can lead to unauthorized information disclosure, theft, or damage to [[computer hardware|hardware]], [[software]], or [[Data (computing)|data]], as well as to the disruption or misdirection of the [[Service (economics)|services]] they provide.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last1=Schatz |first1=Daniel |last2=Bashroush |first2=Rabih |last3=Wall |first3=Julie |date=2017 |title=Towards a More Representative Definition of Cyber Security |url=https://commons.erau.edu/jdfsl/vol12/iss2/8/ |journal=Journal of Digital Forensics, Security and Law |language=en |volume=12 |issue=2 |issn=1558-7215}}</ref><ref>{{Britannica|130682}}</ref>

The growing significance of computer security reflects the increasing dependence on [[computer systems]], the [[Internet]],<ref>{{Cite news |last=Tate |first=Nick |date=7 May 2013 |title=Reliance spells end of road for ICT amateurs |newspaper=The Australian |url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/news/reliance-spells-end-of-road-for-ict-amateurs/news-story/6f84ad403b8721100f5957a472a945eb |url-access=subscription}}</ref> and evolving [[wireless network standards]]. This reliance has expanded with the proliferation of [[smart device]]s, including [[smartphone]]s, [[television]]s, and other components of the [[Internet of things]] (IoT).

As digital infrastructure becomes more embedded in everyday life, cybersecurity has emerged as a critical concern. The complexity of modern [[information systems]]—and the societal functions they underpin—has introduced new vulnerabilities. Systems that manage essential services, such as [[Electric power distribution|power grids]], [[Election security|electoral processes]], and [[finance]], are particularly sensitive to security breaches.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kianpour |first1=Mazaher |last2=Kowalski |first2=Stewart |last3=Øverby |first3=Harald |date=2021 |title=Systematically Understanding Cybersecurity Economics: A Survey |journal=Sustainability |volume=13 |issue=24 |article-number=13677 |doi=10.3390/su132413677 |doi-access=free|bibcode=2021Sust...1313677K |hdl=11250/2978306 |hdl-access=free | issn=2071-1050 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Stevens |first1=Tim |date=11 June 2018 |title=Global Cybersecurity: New Directions in Theory and Methods |url=https://kclpure.kcl.ac.uk/portal/files/97261726/PaG_6_2_Global_Cybersecurity_New_Directions_in_Theory_and_Methods.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190904151257/https://kclpure.kcl.ac.uk/portal/files/97261726/PaG_6_2_Global_Cybersecurity_New_Directions_in_Theory_and_Methods.pdf |archive-date=2019-09-04 |url-status=live |journal=Politics and Governance |volume=6 |issue=2 |pages=1–4 |doi=10.17645/pag.v6i2.1569 |doi-access=free}}</ref> Estimates of global information security spending in 2026 range from US$244 billion to US$308 billion.<ref>
* {{cite web |title=Forecast Analysis: Information Security, Worldwide, 2026 |url=https://www.gartner.com/en/documents/7408930 |publisher=[[Gartner]] |date=5 February 2026 |access-date=2 October 2026}}
* {{cite web |title=Global Security Spend to Exceed $300 Billion in 2026 as the Adoption of AI-Driven Security Platforms Gains Momentum |url=https://www.idc.com/resource-center/press-releases/wwsecuritysg/ |publisher=[[International Data Corporation|IDC]] |date=3 March 2026 |access-date=2 October 2026}}</ref>     

Although many aspects of computer security involve digital security, such as electronic [[passwords]] and [[encryption]], [[physical security]] measures, such as [[Lock and key|metal locks]], are still used to prevent unauthorized tampering. IT security is not a perfect subset of [[information security]] and therefore does not  completely align with the [[security convergence]] schema.

==Vulnerabilities and attacks==
{{Main|Vulnerability (computing)}}

A vulnerability refers to a flaw in the structure, execution, functioning, or internal oversight of a computer or system that compromises its security. Most of the vulnerabilities that have been discovered are documented in the [[Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures]] (CVE) database.<ref>{{Cite web |title=About the CVE Program |url=https://www.cve.org/About/Overview |access-date=2023-04-12 |website=www.cve.org}}</ref> An ''exploitable'' vulnerability is one for which at least one working ''[[Exploit (computer security)|exploit]]'' exists.<ref>{{cite conference | last=Zlatanov | first=Nikola |title=Computer Security and Mobile Security Challenges |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298807979 |conference=Tech Security Conference At: San Francisco, CA  |date=3 December 2015 }}</ref> A ''[[Threat (computer security)|threat]]'' is an action or event that potentially affects hardware, software, or data negatively. A ''threat actor'' is a person or entity that performs a threat (the term ''[[hacker]]'' is more commonly used in popular media), likely by exploiting some vulnerability. Vulnerabilities can be researched, reverse-engineered, hunted, or exploited using [[Automated threat|automated tools]] or customized scripts.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ghidra |url=https://www.nsa.gov/resources/everyone/ghidra/ |access-date=17 August 2020 |archive-date=15 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200815201448/https://www.nsa.gov/resources/everyone/ghidra/ | website=nsa.gov | date=1 August 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Larabel |first=Michael |date=2017-12-28 |title=Syzbot: Google Continuously Fuzzing The Linux Kernel |url=https://www.phoronix.com/scan.php?page=news_item&px=Syzbot-Linux-Kernel-Fuzzing/ |access-date=2021-03-25 |website=www.phoronix.com/ |language=en-US}}</ref>

Various people or parties are vulnerable to [[cyberattack]]s; however, different groups are likely to experience different types of attacks more than others.<ref name="crowdstrike.com">{{Cite web |title=Cyber attacks on SMBs: Current Stats and How to Prevent Them |url=https://www.crowdstrike.com/solutions/small-business/cyber-attacks-on-smbs/ |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=crowdstrike.com |language=en}}</ref>

In April 2023, the [[United Kingdom Government|United Kingdom]] Department for Science, Innovation & Technology released a report on cyberattacks over the previous 12 months.<ref name="Cyber breaches 2023">{{Cite web |title=Cyber security breaches survey 2023 |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/cyber-security-breaches-survey-2023/cyber-security-breaches-survey-2023 |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=GOV.UK |language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231220133957/https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/cyber-security-breaches-survey-2023/cyber-security-breaches-survey-2023|archive-date=2023-12-20}}</ref> They surveyed 2,263 UK businesses, 1,174 UK registered charities, and 554 education institutions. The research found that "32% of businesses and 24% of charities overall recall any breaches or attacks from the last 12 months." These figures were much higher for "medium businesses (59%), large businesses (69%), and high-income charities with £500,000 or more in annual income (56%)."<ref name="Cyber breaches 2023" /> Yet, although medium or large businesses are more often the target, [[Small and medium-sized enterprises|small and midsize businesses]] (SMBs) have become increasingly vulnerable as they often "do not have advanced tools to defend the business" .<ref name="crowdstrike.com" /> SMBs are most likely to be affected by malware, ransomware, phishing, [[man-in-the-middle attack]]s, and Denial-of Service (DoS) Attacks.<ref name="crowdstrike.com" />

Domestic internet users are most likely to be affected by untargeted cyberattacks.<ref name="Cyber attacks">{{Cite web |title=How cyber attacks work |url=https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/information/how-cyber-attacks-work |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=www.ncsc.gov.uk |language=en}}</ref> These are where attackers indiscriminately target as many devices, services, or users as possible. They do this using techniques that take advantage of the openness of the Internet. These strategies mostly include [[phishing]], [[ransomware]], [[Watering hole attack|water holing]] and scanning.<ref name="Cyber attacks" />

To secure a computer system, it is important to understand the attacks that can be made against it, and these [[threat (computer)|threats]] can typically be classified into one of the following categories:

===Backdoor===
A [[Backdoor (computing)|backdoor]] in a computer system, a [[cryptosystem]] or an [[algorithm]], is any secret method of bypassing normal [[authentication]] or security controls. These weaknesses may exist for many reasons, including original design or poor configuration.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-11-30 |title=What is a backdoor attack? Definition and prevention {{!}} NordVPN |url=https://nordvpn.com/blog/backdoor-attack/ |access-date=2024-01-03 |website=nordvpn.com |language=en}}</ref> Due to the nature of backdoors, they are of greater concern to companies and databases as opposed to individuals.

Backdoors may be added by an authorized party to allow some legitimate access or by an attacker for malicious reasons. [[Cybercrime|Criminals]] often use [[malware]] to install backdoors, giving them remote administrative access to a system.<ref name="McAfee-2023">{{Cite web |date=December 4, 2023 |title=What is a backdoor attack? |url=https://www.mcafee.com/learn/backdoor-threat/ |access-date=December 4, 2023 |website=McAfee}}</ref> Once they have access, cybercriminals can "modify files, steal personal information, install unwanted software, and even take control of the entire computer."<ref name="McAfee-2023" />

Backdoors can be difficult to detect, as they often remain hidden within source code or system firmware and may require intimate knowledge of the [[operating system]] to identify.

=== Denial-of-service attack ===
[[Denial-of-service attacks]] (DoS) are designed to make a machine or network resource unavailable to its intended users.<ref name="DoS guidance">{{Cite web |title=Denial of Service (DoS) guidance |url=https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/denial-service-dos-guidance-collection |access-date=2023-12-04 |website=www.ncsc.gov.uk |date=16 March 2016 |language=en}}</ref> Attackers can deny service to individual victims, such as by deliberately entering an incorrect password enough consecutive times to cause the victim's account to be locked, or they may overload the capabilities of a machine or network and block all users at once. While a network attack from a single [[IP address]] can be blocked by adding a new firewall rule, many forms of [[Denial-of-service attack#Distributed DoS|distributed denial-of-service]] (DDoS) attacks are possible, where the attack comes from a large number of points. In this case, defending against these attacks is much more difficult. Such attacks can originate from the [[zombie computer]]s of a [[botnet]] or from a range of other possible techniques, including [[Denial-of-service attack#Reflected attack|distributed reflective denial-of-service]] (DRDoS), where innocent systems are fooled into sending traffic to the victim.<ref name="DoS guidance" /> With such attacks, the amplification factor makes the attack easier for the attacker because they have to use little bandwidth themselves. To understand why attackers may carry out these attacks, see the 'attacker motivation' section.

=== Physical access attacks===
{{main|Physical access}}
A direct-access attack is when an unauthorized user (an attacker) gains physical access to a computer, typically to copy data from it or steal information.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Computer Security |url=https://www.interelectronix.com/computer-security.html |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=www.interelectronix.com}}</ref> Attackers may also compromise security by making operating system modifications, installing [[Computer worm|software worms]], [[keyloggers]], [[covert listening device]]s or using wireless microphones. Even when the system is protected by standard security measures, these may be bypassed by booting another operating system or tool from a [[CD-ROM]] or other bootable media. [[Disk encryption]] and the [[Trusted Platform Module]] standard are designed to prevent these attacks.

Direct service attackers are related in concept to [[DMA attack|direct memory attacks]] which allow an attacker to gain direct access to a computer's memory.<ref name="Kroll">{{Cite web |title=What Is a DMA Attack? Analysis & Mitigation |url=https://www.kroll.com/en/insights/publications/cyber/what-is-dma-attack-understanding-mitigating-threat |access-date=2023-12-04 |website=Kroll |language=en}}</ref> The attacks "take advantage of a feature of modern computers that allows certain devices, such as external hard drives, graphics cards, or network cards, to access the computer's memory directly."<ref name="Kroll" />

===Eavesdropping===
{{main article|Network eavesdropping}}

[[Eavesdropping]] is the act of surreptitiously listening to a private computer conversation (communication), usually between hosts on a network.
